Final thoughts: the code above evaluated whether a Generalized Pareto Distribution (GPD), fit via peaks-over-threshold, would better represent the tail of the burned-area distribution than the Gamma currently used in the extreme-fire sub-model. Threshold stability diagnostics (mean residual life plot; parameter stability across thresholds 50–500 km²) indicated that the shape parameter stabilizes in the range of approximately 250–300 km², closely consistent with the 95th-percentile threshold (254.3 km²) already used to define the extreme-fire regime, supporting the current threshold choice as a reasonable, data-consistent cutoff rather than an arbitrary choice.

GDP-implied cutoff: an estimate of the theoretical upper bound on burned area implied by the fitted tail. For a Generalized Pareto Distribution with shape parameter ξ < 0 (a bounded, Weibull-type tail), the distribution has a finite right endpoint, computed directly from the fitted scale (σ) and shape parameters as threshold − σ/ξ. At a threshold set to 254.3 km² (chosen from 95% cutoff), this implied a cutoff estimate for the maximum burned area of approximately 8,583 km², four times larger than the largest fire actually observed in the training record (2,176 km²). This is not evidence of model misspecification; it reflects a 10-year observational window that contains only 52 fires classified as extreme, has almost certainly not sampled the true upper range of fire sizes the underlying physical process is capable of producing. The GPD's implied cutoff formalizes this limitation, offering a data-driven estimate of how much larger an extreme fire event could plausibly be, beyond anything captured in the data used to train the model.

When interpreting the extreme-fire Gamma component's behavior during posterior sampling: the Gamma distribution's support is unbounded, so draws from the extreme-fire model occasionally exceed the observed historical maximum , up to 6,000 km² in some posterior draws. Rather than treating these as implausible outliers or evidence of poor model behavior, the GPD-implied cutoff suggests such draws are physically reasonable: they remain comfortably below the 8,583 km² ceiling independently estimated from extreme value theory, and are consistent with the possibility of a fire larger than any yet observed occurring within the range the data support. The Gamma distribution's unbounded sampling remains within the implied threshold; artificially capping predicted burned area at the historical maximum would understate legitimate tail uncertainty that the GPD analysis independently identifies

########################
# ----- Fit models ----#
########################
1. Log-normal OLS (baseline) - simplest approach. take log of the outcome and fit a simple linear model
2. Gamma GLM with log link - positive right skewed data. multiplicative affect, ie. 1 unit increase in rh multiplies expected burned area by exp(beta)
3. Bayesian log-normal regression (Stan) - With 178 observations and 11 predictors, the Normal(0,1) priors on standardised coefficients act as ridge regularisation, preventing overfitting
4. Bayesian Gamma regression (Stan) - similar to log normal model (1) but the Gamma likelihood is more appropriate if the variance scales with the mean
5. Two-componenet Mixture Model: splits fires into "extreme" (top 5% by burned area, threshold computed from train only) vs. "typical", with separate Gamma models fit to each subset, combined via the classification probability.

```{r}
##############################################################################
#
# Unified function for fitting burned area models.
# Follows the same structure as ignition_model_functions.R.
#
# Methods:
#   "lognormal_ols"   : OLS on log-transformed outcome (baseline)
#   "gamma_glm"       : Gamma GLM with log link
#   "bayes_lognormal" : Bayesian log-normal regression (RStan)
#   "bayes_gamma"     : Bayesian Gamma regression (RStan)
#
# Train/test split performed OUTSIDE this function.
# Pass pre-standardised train and test sets.
# Outcome variable: burned_area_km2_total (must be > 0 for all rows)
##############################################################################


options(mc.cores = parallel::detectCores())
rstan_options(auto_write = TRUE)

# ── Shared helper functions ───────────────────────────────────────────────────

compute_burned_metrics <- function(y_true, y_pred,
                                    n_boot = 1000, seed = 123) {
  # Performance metrics for a continuous positive outcome
  # y_true / y_pred: burned area in km² (original scale, not log)

  rmse_val  <- sqrt(mean((y_pred - y_true)^2))
  nrmse_val <- rmse_val / mean(y_true)
  cor_val   <- cor(y_pred,  y_true)
  spear_val <- cor(y_pred,  y_true, method = "spearman")
  r2_val    <- 1 - sum((y_true - y_pred)^2) /
                   sum((y_true - mean(y_true))^2)
  mae_val   <- mean(abs(y_pred - y_true))

  # Also compute on log scale (more stable for skewed data)
  log_cor_val   <- cor(log(y_pred + 1), log(y_true + 1))
  log_rmse_val  <- sqrt(mean((log(y_pred + 1) - log(y_true + 1))^2))

  # Bootstrap CIs
  set.seed(seed)
  n        <- length(y_true)
  boot_mat <- matrix(
    NA_real_, nrow = n_boot, ncol = 7,
    dimnames = list(NULL, c("nrmse","cor","spear","r2","mae",
                             "log_cor","log_rmse"))
  )

  for (b in seq_len(n_boot)) {
    idx  <- sample.int(n, n, replace = TRUE)
    y_t  <- y_true[idx]
    y_p  <- y_pred[idx]
    boot_mat[b, "nrmse"]    <- sqrt(mean((y_p - y_t)^2)) / mean(y_t)
    boot_mat[b, "cor"]      <- tryCatch(cor(y_p, y_t),
                                         error = function(e) NA_real_)
    boot_mat[b, "spear"]    <- tryCatch(cor(y_p, y_t, method = "spearman"),
                                         error = function(e) NA_real_)
    boot_mat[b, "r2"]       <- 1 - sum((y_t - y_p)^2) /
                                    sum((y_t - mean(y_t))^2)
    boot_mat[b, "mae"]      <- mean(abs(y_p - y_t))
    boot_mat[b, "log_cor"]  <- tryCatch(
      cor(log(y_p + 1), log(y_t + 1)), error = function(e) NA_real_)
    boot_mat[b, "log_rmse"] <- sqrt(mean((log(y_p + 1) - log(y_t + 1))^2))
  }

  qfun <- function(x) quantile(x[is.finite(x)], probs = c(0.025, 0.975),
                                na.rm = TRUE)

  list(
    nrmse    = nrmse_val,  nrmse_ci   = qfun(boot_mat[, "nrmse"]),
    cor      = cor_val,    cor_ci     = qfun(boot_mat[, "cor"]),
    spearman = spear_val,  spear_ci   = qfun(boot_mat[, "spear"]),
    r2       = r2_val,     r2_ci      = qfun(boot_mat[, "r2"]),
    mae      = mae_val,    mae_ci     = qfun(boot_mat[, "mae"]),
    log_cor  = log_cor_val,log_cor_ci = qfun(boot_mat[, "log_cor"]),
    log_rmse = log_rmse_val,log_rmse_ci = qfun(boot_mat[, "log_rmse"])
  )
}

run_or_load_model <- function(path, fit_expr, verbose = TRUE) {
  if (file.exists(path)) {
    if (verbose) message("Loading saved model from: ", path)
    readRDS(path)
  } else {
    if (verbose) message("Fitting model (cache not found): ", path)
    fit <- eval.parent(substitute(fit_expr))
    dir.create(dirname(path), recursive = TRUE, showWarnings = FALSE)
    if (verbose) message("Saving model to: ", path)
    saveRDS(fit, path)
    fit
  }
}

# ── Stan model code ───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────

# Log-normal: log(y) ~ Normal(alpha + X*beta, sigma)
# Equivalent to y ~ LogNormal(alpha + X*beta, sigma)
.stan_lognormal <- "
data {
  int<lower=1> N;
  int<lower=1> K;
  matrix[N, K] X;
  vector<lower=0>[N] y;
  real<lower=0> sigma_beta;
  real<lower=0> sigma_alpha;
}
parameters {
  real alpha;
  vector[K] beta;
  real<lower=0> sigma;
}
model {
  alpha ~ normal(0, sigma_alpha);
  beta  ~ normal(0, sigma_beta);
  sigma ~ exponential(1);
  log(y) ~ normal(alpha + X * beta, sigma);
}
generated quantities {
  vector[N] log_lik;
  vector[N] y_pred;
  for (n in 1:N) {
    real mu_n   = alpha + dot_product(X[n], beta);
    log_lik[n]  = normal_lpdf(log(y[n]) | mu_n, sigma);
    // Back-transform with log-normal bias correction
    // E[Y] = exp(mu + sigma^2/2)
    y_pred[n]   = exp(mu_n + 0.5 * sigma^2);
  }
}"

# Gamma GLM: y ~ Gamma(shape, rate)
# log(E[y]) = alpha + X*beta
# Parameterised via mean mu and shape phi
.stan_gamma <- "
data {
  int<lower=1> N;
  int<lower=1> K;
  matrix[N, K] X;
  vector<lower=0>[N] y;
  real<lower=0> sigma_beta;
  real<lower=0> sigma_alpha;
}
parameters {
  real alpha;
  vector[K] beta;
  real<lower=0> phi;   // shape / concentration parameter
}
model {
  alpha ~ normal(0, sigma_alpha);
  beta  ~ normal(0, sigma_beta);
  phi   ~ exponential(0.1);   // weakly informative — allows large shapes
  for (n in 1:N) {
    real mu_n = exp(alpha + dot_product(X[n], beta));
    y[n] ~ gamma(phi, phi / mu_n);
  }
}
generated quantities {
  vector[N] log_lik;
  vector[N] y_pred;
  for (n in 1:N) {
    real mu_n  = exp(alpha + dot_product(X[n], beta));
    log_lik[n] = gamma_lpdf(y[n] | phi, phi / mu_n);
    y_pred[n]  = mu_n;   // posterior mean prediction
  }
}"

# ── Main function ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────

fit_burned_area_model <- function(train,
                                   test,
                                   predictors,
                                   outcome         = "burned_area_km2_total",
                                   method          = c("lognormal_ols",
                                                       "gamma_glm",
                                                       "bayes_lognormal",
                                                       "bayes_gamma"),
                                   sigma_beta      = 1,
                                   sigma_alpha     = 5,
                                   iter            = 2000,
                                   chains          = 4,
                                   seed            = 123,
                                   n_boot          = 1000,
                                   compiled_model  = NULL) {
  # ── Args ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
  # train / test   : pre-standardised data; must contain outcome and predictors
  # predictors     : character vector of predictor column names
  # outcome        : name of outcome column (default "burned_area_km2_total")
  # method         : one of "lognormal_ols", "gamma_glm",
  #                          "bayes_lognormal", "bayes_gamma"
  # sigma_beta     : prior SD for regression coefficients (Bayesian only)
  # sigma_alpha    : prior SD for intercept (Bayesian only)
  # iter / chains  : Stan sampling settings (Bayesian only)
  # seed           : random seed
  # n_boot         : bootstrap resamples for confidence intervals
  # compiled_model : pre-compiled Stan model (Bayesian only)

  method <- match.arg(method)

  # Validate outcome is positive (required for Gamma and log-normal)
  if (any(train[[outcome]] <= 0)) {
    stop(sprintf(
      "All values of '%s' must be > 0. Found %d non-positive values.",
      outcome, sum(train[[outcome]] <= 0)
    ))
  }

  cat(sprintf("[%s] Training rows : %d\n", method, nrow(train)))
  cat(sprintf("[%s] Test rows     : %d\n", method, nrow(test)))
  cat(sprintf("[%s] Outcome range : %.2f – %.2f km²\n",
              method, min(train[[outcome]]), max(train[[outcome]])))

  y_train <- train[[outcome]]
  y_test  <- test[[outcome]]

  # ── Formula objects ───────────────────────────────────────────────────────
  formula_obj <- as.formula(
    paste(outcome, "~", paste(predictors, collapse = " + "))
  )
  formula_matrix <- as.formula(
    paste("~", paste(predictors, collapse = " + "), "- 1")
  )

  # Initialise
  fit        <- NULL
  coef_table <- NULL
  p_hat      <- NULL    # predictions on original km² scale
  extra      <- list()

  # ══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
  # 1. Log-normal OLS
  # ══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════

  if (method == "lognormal_ols") {

    cat("[lognormal_ols] Fitting OLS on log(burned_area)...\n")

    train_log        <- train
    train_log$log_y  <- log(train[[outcome]])
    test_log         <- test
    test_log$log_y   <- log(test[[outcome]])

    formula_log <- as.formula(
      paste("log_y ~", paste(predictors, collapse = " + "))
    )

    fit <- lm(formula_log, data = train_log)

    coef_table           <- as.data.frame(summary(fit)$coefficients)
    coef_table$variable  <- rownames(coef_table)
    rownames(coef_table) <- NULL

    # Back-transform with log-normal bias correction: E[Y] = exp(mu + sigma²/2)
    sigma_hat <- summary(fit)$sigma
    log_pred  <- predict(fit, newdata = test_log)
    p_hat     <- exp(log_pred + 0.5 * sigma_hat^2)

    extra$sigma_hat   <- sigma_hat
    extra$log_pred    <- log_pred
    extra$aic         <- AIC(fit)
    cat(sprintf("[lognormal_ols] Sigma (log scale): %.4f | AIC: %.2f\n",
                sigma_hat, AIC(fit)))
  }

  # ══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
  # 2. Gamma GLM with log link
  # ══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════

  if (method == "gamma_glm") {

    cat("[gamma_glm] Fitting Gamma GLM with log link...\n")

    fit <- glm(formula_obj,
               data   = train,
               family = Gamma(link = "log"))

    coef_table           <- as.data.frame(summary(fit)$coefficients)
    coef_table$variable  <- rownames(coef_table)
    rownames(coef_table) <- NULL

    p_hat      <- predict(fit, newdata = test, type = "response")
    extra$aic  <- AIC(fit)

    # Dispersion estimate
    extra$dispersion <- summary(fit)$dispersion
    cat(sprintf("[gamma_glm] Dispersion: %.4f | AIC: %.2f\n",
                extra$dispersion, AIC(fit)))
  }

  # ══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
  # 3 & 4. Bayesian models (log-normal or Gamma)
  # ══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════

  if (method %in% c("bayes_lognormal", "bayes_gamma")) {

    stan_code <- if (method == "bayes_lognormal") {
      .stan_lognormal
    } else {
      .stan_gamma
    }

    X_train <- model.matrix(formula_matrix, data = train)
    X_test  <- model.matrix(formula_matrix, data = test)

    stan_data <- list(
      N           = nrow(train),
      K           = ncol(X_train),
      X           = X_train,
      y           = y_train,
      sigma_beta  = sigma_beta,
      sigma_alpha = sigma_alpha
    )

    # Compile (once per session)
    if (is.null(compiled_model)) {
      cat(sprintf("[%s] Compiling Stan model...\n", method))
      compiled_model <- compiled_model <- stan_model(
        model_code = stan_code,
        model_name = paste0("burned_area_", method, "_",
                            digest::digest(predictors)))
    }

    cat(sprintf("[%s] Sampling (%d chains × %d iter)...\n",
                method, chains, iter))
    fit <- sampling(
      compiled_model,
      data    = stan_data,
      iter    = iter,
      chains  = chains,
      seed    = seed,
      control = list(adapt_delta = 0.95),
      refresh = 200
    )

    # Convergence check
    rhat_vals <- summary(fit)$summary[, "Rhat"]
    max_rhat  <- max(rhat_vals, na.rm = TRUE)
    cat(sprintf("[%s] Max R-hat: %.4f %s\n",
                method, max_rhat,
                ifelse(max_rhat > 1.01, "⚠ CONVERGENCE WARNING", "✓")))

    # LOO-CV
    loo_result <- tryCatch(
      loo(fit, pars = "log_lik"),
      error = function(e) {
        message("LOO-CV failed: ", e$message)
        NULL
      }
    )
    extra$loo        <- loo_result
    extra$max_rhat   <- max_rhat
    extra$compiled_model <- compiled_model

    # Posterior summaries
    pars_to_summarise <- if (method == "bayes_lognormal") {
      c("alpha", "beta", "sigma")
    } else {
      c("alpha", "beta", "phi")
    }

    summ <- summary(fit, pars = pars_to_summarise,
                     probs = c(0.025, 0.25, 0.5, 0.75, 0.975))$summary

    alpha_mean <- summ["alpha", "mean"]
    beta_rows  <- grep("^beta\\[", rownames(summ))
    beta_means <- summ[beta_rows, "mean"]
    names(beta_means) <- colnames(X_train)

    coef_table           <- as.data.frame(summ)
    coef_table$variable  <- rownames(summ)
    rownames(coef_table) <- NULL

    extra$coef_means <- list(alpha = alpha_mean, beta = beta_means)

    # Posterior predictions on test set (posterior mean of y_pred draws)
    post   <- rstan::extract(fit)

    # Generate predictions for test set from posterior draws
    n_draws    <- length(post$alpha)
    pred_draws <- matrix(NA_real_, nrow = nrow(test), ncol = n_draws)

    for (d in seq_len(n_draws)) {
      mu_d <- post$alpha[d] + X_test %*% post$beta[d, ]
      if (method == "bayes_lognormal") {
        sigma_d       <- post$sigma[d]
        pred_draws[, d] <- exp(mu_d + 0.5 * sigma_d^2)
      } else {
        pred_draws[, d] <- exp(mu_d)   # Gamma mean = exp(linear predictor)
      }
    }

    p_hat  <- rowMeans(pred_draws)   # posterior mean prediction
    p_sd   <- apply(pred_draws, 1, sd)
    p_low  <- apply(pred_draws, 1, quantile, 0.025)
    p_high <- apply(pred_draws, 1, quantile, 0.975)

    extra$pred_sd   <- p_sd
    extra$pred_low  <- p_low
    extra$pred_high <- p_high
  }

  # ══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
  # Shared: metrics and output
  # ══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════

  metrics <- compute_burned_metrics(y_test, p_hat,
                                     n_boot = n_boot, seed = seed)

  cat(sprintf("[%s] nRMSE    : %.4f (%.4f, %.4f)\n",
              method, metrics$nrmse,   metrics$nrmse_ci[1],   metrics$nrmse_ci[2]))
  cat(sprintf("[%s] Pearson r: %.4f (%.4f, %.4f)\n",
              method, metrics$cor,     metrics$cor_ci[1],     metrics$cor_ci[2]))
  cat(sprintf("[%s] Spearman : %.4f (%.4f, %.4f)\n",
              method, metrics$spearman,metrics$spear_ci[1],   metrics$spear_ci[2]))
  cat(sprintf("[%s] R²       : %.4f (%.4f, %.4f)\n",
              method, metrics$r2,      metrics$r2_ci[1],      metrics$r2_ci[2]))
  cat(sprintf("[%s] MAE (km²): %.2f  (%.2f, %.2f)\n",
              method, metrics$mae,     metrics$mae_ci[1],     metrics$mae_ci[2]))
  cat(sprintf("[%s] Log corr : %.4f (%.4f, %.4f)\n",
              method, metrics$log_cor, metrics$log_cor_ci[1], metrics$log_cor_ci[2]))

  # Prediction data frame
  pred_df <- data.frame(
    lat                   = test$lat,
    lon                   = test$lon,
    year                  = test$year,
    month                 = test$month,
    burned_area_km2_total = y_test,
    burned_area_pred      = p_hat,
    residual              = y_test - p_hat,
    log_residual          = log(y_test + 1) - log(p_hat + 1)
  )

  # Add posterior uncertainty columns for Bayesian models
  if (!is.null(extra$pred_sd)) {
    pred_df$pred_sd   <- extra$pred_sd
    pred_df$pred_low  <- extra$pred_low
    pred_df$pred_high <- extra$pred_high
  }

  c(
    list(
      method      = method,
      predictors  = predictors,
      outcome     = outcome,
      fit         = fit,
      coef_table  = coef_table,
      predictions = pred_df,
      metrics     = metrics
    ),
    extra   # appends aic, dispersion, loo, max_rhat, compiled_model, etc.
  )
}

# ── Convenience: compare metrics across fitted models ─────────────────────────

compare_burned_models <- function(model_list) {
  do.call(rbind, lapply(model_list, function(m) {
    mt <- m$metrics
    data.frame(
      method       = m$method,
      predictors   = paste(m$predictors, collapse = ", "),
      nrmse        = mt$nrmse,
      nrmse_low    = mt$nrmse_ci[1],
      nrmse_high   = mt$nrmse_ci[2],
      cor          = mt$cor,
      cor_low      = mt$cor_ci[1],
      cor_high     = mt$cor_ci[2],
      spearman     = mt$spearman,
      spear_low    = mt$spear_ci[1],
      spear_high   = mt$spear_ci[2],
      r2           = mt$r2,
      r2_low       = mt$r2_ci[1],
      r2_high      = mt$r2_ci[2],
      mae          = mt$mae,
      mae_low      = mt$mae_ci[1],
      mae_high     = mt$mae_ci[2],
      log_cor      = mt$log_cor,
      log_cor_low  = mt$log_cor_ci[1],
      log_cor_high = mt$log_cor_ci[2],
      row.names    = NULL
    )
  }))
}

```

Mixture model:
```{r}
##############################################################################
#
# Unified function for fitting burned area models.
# Follows the same structure as ignition_model_functions.R.
#
# Methods:
#   "lognormal_ols"     : OLS on log-transformed outcome (baseline)
#   "gamma_glm"         : Gamma GLM with log link
#   "bayes_lognormal"   : Bayesian log-normal regression (RStan)
#   "bayes_gamma"       : Bayesian Gamma regression (RStan)
#   "bayes_mixture_gamma": Two-component mixture — Bayesian logistic
#                          classifier for extreme (top 5%) vs typical fires,
#                          combined with separate Bayesian Gamma magnitude
#                          models fit to each subset
#
# Train/test split performed OUTSIDE this function.
# Pass pre-standardised train and test sets.
# Outcome variable: burned_area_km2_total (must be > 0 for all rows)
##############################################################################


options(mc.cores = parallel::detectCores())
rstan_options(auto_write = TRUE)

# ── Shared helper functions ───────────────────────────────────────────────────

compute_burned_metrics <- function(y_true, y_pred,
                                    n_boot = 1000, seed = 123) {
  # Performance metrics for a continuous positive outcome
  # y_true / y_pred: burned area in km² (original scale, not log)

  rmse_val  <- sqrt(mean((y_pred - y_true)^2))
  nrmse_val <- rmse_val / mean(y_true)
  cor_val   <- cor(y_pred,  y_true)
  spear_val <- cor(y_pred,  y_true, method = "spearman")
  r2_val    <- 1 - sum((y_true - y_pred)^2) /
                   sum((y_true - mean(y_true))^2)
  mae_val   <- mean(abs(y_pred - y_true))

  # Also compute on log scale (more stable for skewed data)
  log_cor_val   <- cor(log(y_pred + 1), log(y_true + 1))
  log_rmse_val  <- sqrt(mean((log(y_pred + 1) - log(y_true + 1))^2))

  # Bootstrap CIs
  set.seed(seed)
  n        <- length(y_true)
  boot_mat <- matrix(
    NA_real_, nrow = n_boot, ncol = 7,
    dimnames = list(NULL, c("nrmse","cor","spear","r2","mae",
                             "log_cor","log_rmse"))
  )

  for (b in seq_len(n_boot)) {
    idx  <- sample.int(n, n, replace = TRUE)
    y_t  <- y_true[idx]
    y_p  <- y_pred[idx]
    boot_mat[b, "nrmse"]    <- sqrt(mean((y_p - y_t)^2)) / mean(y_t)
    boot_mat[b, "cor"]      <- tryCatch(cor(y_p, y_t),
                                         error = function(e) NA_real_)
    boot_mat[b, "spear"]    <- tryCatch(cor(y_p, y_t, method = "spearman"),
                                         error = function(e) NA_real_)
    boot_mat[b, "r2"]       <- 1 - sum((y_t - y_p)^2) /
                                    sum((y_t - mean(y_t))^2)
    boot_mat[b, "mae"]      <- mean(abs(y_p - y_t))
    boot_mat[b, "log_cor"]  <- tryCatch(
      cor(log(y_p + 1), log(y_t + 1)), error = function(e) NA_real_)
    boot_mat[b, "log_rmse"] <- sqrt(mean((log(y_p + 1) - log(y_t + 1))^2))
  }

  qfun <- function(x) quantile(x[is.finite(x)], probs = c(0.025, 0.975),
                                na.rm = TRUE)

  list(
    nrmse    = nrmse_val,  nrmse_ci   = qfun(boot_mat[, "nrmse"]),
    cor      = cor_val,    cor_ci     = qfun(boot_mat[, "cor"]),
    spearman = spear_val,  spear_ci   = qfun(boot_mat[, "spear"]),
    r2       = r2_val,     r2_ci      = qfun(boot_mat[, "r2"]),
    mae      = mae_val,    mae_ci     = qfun(boot_mat[, "mae"]),
    log_cor  = log_cor_val,log_cor_ci = qfun(boot_mat[, "log_cor"]),
    log_rmse = log_rmse_val,log_rmse_ci = qfun(boot_mat[, "log_rmse"])
  )
}

run_or_load_model <- function(path, fit_expr, verbose = TRUE) {
  if (file.exists(path)) {
    if (verbose) message("Loading saved model from: ", path)
    readRDS(path)
  } else {
    if (verbose) message("Fitting model (cache not found): ", path)
    fit <- eval.parent(substitute(fit_expr))
    dir.create(dirname(path), recursive = TRUE, showWarnings = FALSE)
    if (verbose) message("Saving model to: ", path)
    saveRDS(fit, path)
    fit
  }
}

# ── Stan model code ───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────

# Log-normal: log(y) ~ Normal(alpha + X*beta, sigma)
# Equivalent to y ~ LogNormal(alpha + X*beta, sigma)
.stan_lognormal <- "
data {
  int<lower=1> N;
  int<lower=1> K;
  matrix[N, K] X;
  vector<lower=0>[N] y;
  real<lower=0> sigma_beta;
  real<lower=0> sigma_alpha;
}
parameters {
  real alpha;
  vector[K] beta;
  real<lower=0> sigma;
}
model {
  alpha ~ normal(0, sigma_alpha);
  beta  ~ normal(0, sigma_beta);
  sigma ~ exponential(1);
  log(y) ~ normal(alpha + X * beta, sigma);
}
generated quantities {
  vector[N] log_lik;
  vector[N] y_pred;
  for (n in 1:N) {
    real mu_n   = alpha + dot_product(X[n], beta);
    log_lik[n]  = normal_lpdf(log(y[n]) | mu_n, sigma);
    // Back-transform with log-normal bias correction
    // E[Y] = exp(mu + sigma^2/2)
    y_pred[n]   = exp(mu_n + 0.5 * sigma^2);
  }
}"

# Gamma GLM: y ~ Gamma(shape, rate)
# log(E[y]) = alpha + X*beta
# Parameterised via mean mu and shape phi
.stan_gamma <- "
data {
  int<lower=1> N;
  int<lower=1> K;
  matrix[N, K] X;
  vector<lower=0>[N] y;
  real<lower=0> sigma_beta;
  real<lower=0> sigma_alpha;
}
parameters {
  real alpha;
  vector[K] beta;
  real<lower=0> phi;   // shape / concentration parameter
}
model {
  alpha ~ normal(0, sigma_alpha);
  beta  ~ normal(0, sigma_beta);
  phi   ~ exponential(0.1);   // weakly informative — allows large shapes
  for (n in 1:N) {
    real mu_n = exp(alpha + dot_product(X[n], beta));
    y[n] ~ gamma(phi, phi / mu_n);
  }
}
generated quantities {
  vector[N] log_lik;
  vector[N] y_pred;
  for (n in 1:N) {
    real mu_n  = exp(alpha + dot_product(X[n], beta));
    log_lik[n] = gamma_lpdf(y[n] | phi, phi / mu_n);
    y_pred[n]  = mu_n;   // posterior mean prediction
  }
}"

# Bernoulli classifier: y ~ Bernoulli(inv_logit(alpha + X*beta))
# Used as the "extreme vs typical" classification stage of the mixture model
.stan_bernoulli <- "
data {
  int<lower=1> N;
  int<lower=1> K;
  matrix[N, K] X;
  int<lower=0,upper=1> y[N];
  real<lower=0> sigma_beta;
  real<lower=0> sigma_alpha;
}
parameters {
  real alpha;
  vector[K] beta;
}
model {
  alpha ~ normal(0, sigma_alpha);
  beta  ~ normal(0, sigma_beta);
  y ~ bernoulli_logit(alpha + X * beta);
}
generated quantities {
  vector[N] log_lik;
  for (n in 1:N)
    log_lik[n] = bernoulli_logit_lpmf(y[n] | alpha + dot_product(X[n], beta));
}"

# ── Main function ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────

fit_burned_area_model <- function(train,
                                   test,
                                   predictors,
                                   outcome         = "burned_area_km2_total",
                                   method          = c("lognormal_ols",
                                                       "gamma_glm",
                                                       "bayes_lognormal",
                                                       "bayes_gamma",
                                                       "bayes_mixture_gamma"),
                                   sigma_beta      = 1,
                                   sigma_alpha     = 5,
                                   iter            = 2000,
                                   chains          = 4,
                                   seed            = 123,
                                   n_boot          = 1000,
                                   compiled_model  = NULL,
                                   extreme_quantile = 0.95) {
  # ── Args ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
  # train / test     : pre-standardised data; must contain outcome and predictors
  # predictors       : character vector of predictor column names
  # outcome          : name of outcome column (default "burned_area_km2_total")
  # method           : one of "lognormal_ols", "gamma_glm",
  #                            "bayes_lognormal", "bayes_gamma",
  #                            "bayes_mixture_gamma"
  # sigma_beta       : prior SD for regression coefficients (Bayesian only)
  # sigma_alpha      : prior SD for intercept (Bayesian only)
  # iter / chains    : Stan sampling settings (Bayesian only)
  # seed             : random seed
  # n_boot           : bootstrap resamples for confidence intervals
  # compiled_model   : pre-compiled Stan model (Bayesian only).
  #                     For "bayes_mixture_gamma", pass a named list:
  #                     list(logistic = <stanmodel>, gamma = <stanmodel>)
  # extreme_quantile : quantile (of train outcome) defining "extreme" fires
  #                     for "bayes_mixture_gamma" (default 0.95)

  method <- match.arg(method)

  # Validate outcome is positive (required for Gamma and log-normal)
  if (any(train[[outcome]] <= 0)) {
    stop(sprintf(
      "All values of '%s' must be > 0. Found %d non-positive values.",
      outcome, sum(train[[outcome]] <= 0)
    ))
  }

  cat(sprintf("[%s] Training rows : %d\n", method, nrow(train)))
  cat(sprintf("[%s] Test rows     : %d\n", method, nrow(test)))
  cat(sprintf("[%s] Outcome range : %.2f – %.2f km²\n",
              method, min(train[[outcome]]), max(train[[outcome]])))

  y_train <- train[[outcome]]
  y_test  <- test[[outcome]]

  # ── Formula objects ───────────────────────────────────────────────────────
  formula_obj <- as.formula(
    paste(outcome, "~", paste(predictors, collapse = " + "))
  )
  formula_matrix <- as.formula(
    paste("~", paste(predictors, collapse = " + "), "- 1")
  )

  # Initialise
  fit        <- NULL
  coef_table <- NULL
  p_hat      <- NULL    # predictions on original km² scale
  extra      <- list()

  # ══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
  # 1. Log-normal OLS
  # ══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════

  if (method == "lognormal_ols") {

    cat("[lognormal_ols] Fitting OLS on log(burned_area)...\n")

    train_log        <- train
    train_log$log_y  <- log(train[[outcome]])
    test_log         <- test
    test_log$log_y   <- log(test[[outcome]])

    formula_log <- as.formula(
      paste("log_y ~", paste(predictors, collapse = " + "))
    )

    fit <- lm(formula_log, data = train_log)

    coef_table           <- as.data.frame(summary(fit)$coefficients)
    coef_table$variable  <- rownames(coef_table)
    rownames(coef_table) <- NULL

    # Back-transform with log-normal bias correction: E[Y] = exp(mu + sigma²/2)
    sigma_hat <- summary(fit)$sigma
    log_pred  <- predict(fit, newdata = test_log)
    p_hat     <- exp(log_pred + 0.5 * sigma_hat^2)

    extra$sigma_hat   <- sigma_hat
    extra$log_pred    <- log_pred
    extra$aic         <- AIC(fit)
    cat(sprintf("[lognormal_ols] Sigma (log scale): %.4f | AIC: %.2f\n",
                sigma_hat, AIC(fit)))
  }

  # ══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
  # 2. Gamma GLM with log link
  # ══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════

  if (method == "gamma_glm") {

    cat("[gamma_glm] Fitting Gamma GLM with log link...\n")

    fit <- glm(formula_obj,
               data   = train,
               family = Gamma(link = "log"))

    coef_table           <- as.data.frame(summary(fit)$coefficients)
    coef_table$variable  <- rownames(coef_table)
    rownames(coef_table) <- NULL

    p_hat      <- predict(fit, newdata = test, type = "response")
    extra$aic  <- AIC(fit)

    # Dispersion estimate
    extra$dispersion <- summary(fit)$dispersion
    cat(sprintf("[gamma_glm] Dispersion: %.4f | AIC: %.2f\n",
                extra$dispersion, AIC(fit)))
  }

  # ══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
  # 3 & 4. Bayesian models (log-normal or Gamma)
  # ══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════

  if (method %in% c("bayes_lognormal", "bayes_gamma")) {

    stan_code <- if (method == "bayes_lognormal") {
      .stan_lognormal
    } else {
      .stan_gamma
    }

    X_train <- model.matrix(formula_matrix, data = train)
    X_test  <- model.matrix(formula_matrix, data = test)

    stan_data <- list(
      N           = nrow(train),
      K           = ncol(X_train),
      X           = X_train,
      y           = y_train,
      sigma_beta  = sigma_beta,
      sigma_alpha = sigma_alpha
    )

    # Compile (once per session)
    if (is.null(compiled_model)) {
      cat(sprintf("[%s] Compiling Stan model...\n", method))
      compiled_model <- compiled_model <- stan_model(
        model_code = stan_code,
        model_name = paste0("burned_area_", method, "_",
                            digest::digest(predictors)))
    }

    cat(sprintf("[%s] Sampling (%d chains × %d iter)...\n",
                method, chains, iter))
    fit <- sampling(
      compiled_model,
      data    = stan_data,
      iter    = iter,
      chains  = chains,
      seed    = seed,
      control = list(adapt_delta = 0.95),
      refresh = 200
    )

    # Convergence check
    rhat_vals <- summary(fit)$summary[, "Rhat"]
    max_rhat  <- max(rhat_vals, na.rm = TRUE)
    cat(sprintf("[%s] Max R-hat: %.4f %s\n",
                method, max_rhat,
                ifelse(max_rhat > 1.01, "⚠ CONVERGENCE WARNING", "✓")))

    # LOO-CV
    loo_result <- tryCatch(
      loo(fit, pars = "log_lik"),
      error = function(e) {
        message("LOO-CV failed: ", e$message)
        NULL
      }
    )
    extra$loo        <- loo_result
    extra$max_rhat   <- max_rhat
    extra$compiled_model <- compiled_model

    # Posterior summaries
    pars_to_summarise <- if (method == "bayes_lognormal") {
      c("alpha", "beta", "sigma")
    } else {
      c("alpha", "beta", "phi")
    }

    summ <- summary(fit, pars = pars_to_summarise,
                     probs = c(0.025, 0.25, 0.5, 0.75, 0.975))$summary

    alpha_mean <- summ["alpha", "mean"]
    beta_rows  <- grep("^beta\\[", rownames(summ))
    beta_means <- summ[beta_rows, "mean"]
    names(beta_means) <- colnames(X_train)

    coef_table           <- as.data.frame(summ)
    coef_table$variable  <- rownames(summ)
    rownames(coef_table) <- NULL

    extra$coef_means <- list(alpha = alpha_mean, beta = beta_means)

    # Posterior predictions on test set (posterior mean of y_pred draws)
    post   <- rstan::extract(fit)

    # Generate predictions for test set from posterior draws
    n_draws    <- length(post$alpha)
    pred_draws <- matrix(NA_real_, nrow = nrow(test), ncol = n_draws)

    for (d in seq_len(n_draws)) {
      mu_d <- post$alpha[d] + X_test %*% post$beta[d, ]
      if (method == "bayes_lognormal") {
        sigma_d       <- post$sigma[d]
        pred_draws[, d] <- exp(mu_d + 0.5 * sigma_d^2)
      } else {
        pred_draws[, d] <- exp(mu_d)   # Gamma mean = exp(linear predictor)
      }
    }

    p_hat  <- rowMeans(pred_draws)   # posterior mean prediction
    p_sd   <- apply(pred_draws, 1, sd)
    p_low  <- apply(pred_draws, 1, quantile, 0.025)
    p_high <- apply(pred_draws, 1, quantile, 0.975)

    extra$pred_sd   <- p_sd
    extra$pred_low  <- p_low
    extra$pred_high <- p_high
  }

  # ══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
  # 5. Bayesian mixture: logistic classifier (extreme vs typical) +
  #    separate Gamma magnitude models for each group
  # ══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════

  if (method == "bayes_mixture_gamma") {

    threshold <- quantile(y_train, extreme_quantile)
    cat(sprintf("[bayes_mixture_gamma] Extreme threshold (%.0fth pct of train): %.2f km²\n",
                extreme_quantile * 100, threshold))

    is_extreme_train <- as.integer(y_train >= threshold)
    cat(sprintf("[bayes_mixture_gamma] Extreme fires in train: %d / %d (%.1f%%)\n",
                sum(is_extreme_train), length(is_extreme_train),
                100 * mean(is_extreme_train)))

    X_train <- model.matrix(formula_matrix, data = train)
    X_test  <- model.matrix(formula_matrix, data = test)

    # ── Part 1: classification (extreme vs typical) ─────────────────────────
    stan_data_logit <- list(
      N = nrow(train), K = ncol(X_train), X = X_train,
      y = is_extreme_train,
      sigma_beta = sigma_beta, sigma_alpha = sigma_alpha
    )

    if (is.null(compiled_model) || is.null(compiled_model$logistic)) {
      cat("[bayes_mixture_gamma] Compiling classification (logistic) Stan model...\n")
      sm_logit <- stan_model(
        model_code = .stan_bernoulli,
        model_name = paste0("burned_area_mixture_logit_", digest::digest(predictors))
      )
    } else {
      sm_logit <- compiled_model$logistic
    }

    cat("[bayes_mixture_gamma] Sampling classification model...\n")
    fit_logit <- sampling(sm_logit, data = stan_data_logit,
                           iter = iter, chains = chains, seed = seed,
                           control = list(adapt_delta = 0.95), refresh = 200)

    rhat_logit <- max(summary(fit_logit)$summary[, "Rhat"], na.rm = TRUE)
    cat(sprintf("[bayes_mixture_gamma] Classification max R-hat: %.4f %s\n",
                rhat_logit, ifelse(rhat_logit > 1.01, "⚠ CONVERGENCE WARNING", "✓")))

    # ── Part 2a: magnitude model for EXTREME fires ───────────────────────────
    train_extreme <- train[is_extreme_train == 1, , drop = FALSE]
    y_extreme     <- y_train[is_extreme_train == 1]
    X_extreme     <- model.matrix(formula_matrix, data = train_extreme)

    stan_data_extreme <- list(
      N = nrow(train_extreme), K = ncol(X_extreme), X = X_extreme, y = y_extreme,
      sigma_beta = sigma_beta, sigma_alpha = sigma_alpha
    )

    if (is.null(compiled_model) || is.null(compiled_model$gamma)) {
      cat("[bayes_mixture_gamma] Compiling magnitude (Gamma) Stan model...\n")
      sm_gamma <- stan_model(
        model_code = .stan_gamma,
        model_name = paste0("burned_area_mixture_gamma_", digest::digest(predictors))
      )
    } else {
      sm_gamma <- compiled_model$gamma
    }

    cat(sprintf("[bayes_mixture_gamma] Sampling extreme-fire magnitude model (N=%d)...\n",
                nrow(train_extreme)))
    fit_extreme <- sampling(sm_gamma, data = stan_data_extreme,
                             iter = iter, chains = chains, seed = seed,
                             control = list(adapt_delta = 0.95), refresh = 200)

    rhat_extreme <- max(summary(fit_extreme)$summary[, "Rhat"], na.rm = TRUE)
    cat(sprintf("[bayes_mixture_gamma] Extreme-magnitude max R-hat: %.4f %s\n",
                rhat_extreme, ifelse(rhat_extreme > 1.01, "⚠ CONVERGENCE WARNING", "✓")))

    # ── Part 2b: magnitude model for TYPICAL (non-extreme) fires ────────────
    train_normal <- train[is_extreme_train == 0, , drop = FALSE]
    y_normal     <- y_train[is_extreme_train == 0]
    X_normal     <- model.matrix(formula_matrix, data = train_normal)

    stan_data_normal <- list(
      N = nrow(train_normal), K = ncol(X_normal), X = X_normal, y = y_normal,
      sigma_beta = sigma_beta, sigma_alpha = sigma_alpha
    )

    cat(sprintf("[bayes_mixture_gamma] Sampling typical-fire magnitude model (N=%d)...\n",
                nrow(train_normal)))
    fit_normal <- sampling(sm_gamma, data = stan_data_normal,
                            iter = iter, chains = chains, seed = seed,
                            control = list(adapt_delta = 0.95), refresh = 200)

    rhat_normal <- max(summary(fit_normal)$summary[, "Rhat"], na.rm = TRUE)
    cat(sprintf("[bayes_mixture_gamma] Typical-magnitude max R-hat: %.4f %s\n",
                rhat_normal, ifelse(rhat_normal > 1.01, "⚠ CONVERGENCE WARNING", "✓")))

    max_rhat <- max(rhat_logit, rhat_extreme, rhat_normal, na.rm = TRUE)

    extra$threshold         <- threshold
    extra$extreme_quantile  <- extreme_quantile
    extra$max_rhat          <- max_rhat
    extra$max_rhat_logit    <- rhat_logit
    extra$max_rhat_extreme  <- rhat_extreme
    extra$max_rhat_normal   <- rhat_normal
    extra$compiled_model    <- list(logistic = sm_logit, gamma = sm_gamma)
    extra$fit_logit          <- fit_logit
    extra$fit_extreme        <- fit_extreme
    extra$fit_normal         <- fit_normal
    extra$loo <- NULL  # not computed for mixture — needs a joint log-lik
    cat("[bayes_mixture_gamma] Note: LOO-CV not computed for mixture models (needs a combined joint log-lik).\n")

    # ── Posterior summaries (three components) ───────────────────────────────
    summ_logit   <- summary(fit_logit,   pars = c("alpha", "beta"),
                             probs = c(0.025, 0.25, 0.5, 0.75, 0.975))$summary
    summ_extreme <- summary(fit_extreme, pars = c("alpha", "beta", "phi"),
                             probs = c(0.025, 0.25, 0.5, 0.75, 0.975))$summary
    summ_normal  <- summary(fit_normal,  pars = c("alpha", "beta", "phi"),
                             probs = c(0.025, 0.25, 0.5, 0.75, 0.975))$summary

    coef_table <- rbind(
      transform(as.data.frame(summ_logit),
                variable  = c("alpha", paste0("beta_", colnames(X_train))),
                component = "classification"),
      transform(as.data.frame(summ_extreme),
                variable  = c("alpha", paste0("beta_", colnames(X_extreme)), "phi"),
                component = "magnitude_extreme"),
      transform(as.data.frame(summ_normal),
                variable  = c("alpha", paste0("beta_", colnames(X_normal)), "phi"),
                component = "magnitude_typical")
    )
    rownames(coef_table) <- NULL

    extra$coef_means <- list(
      logistic = list(
        alpha = summ_logit["alpha", "mean"],
        beta  = setNames(summ_logit[grep("^beta\\[", rownames(summ_logit)), "mean"],
                          colnames(X_train))
      ),
      extreme = list(
        alpha = summ_extreme["alpha", "mean"],
        beta  = setNames(summ_extreme[grep("^beta\\[", rownames(summ_extreme)), "mean"],
                          colnames(X_extreme))
      ),
      normal = list(
        alpha = summ_normal["alpha", "mean"],
        beta  = setNames(summ_normal[grep("^beta\\[", rownames(summ_normal)), "mean"],
                          colnames(X_normal))
      )
    )

    # ── Posterior predictions on test set (combine draws from all 3 fits) ───
    post_logit   <- rstan::extract(fit_logit)
    post_extreme <- rstan::extract(fit_extreme)
    post_normal  <- rstan::extract(fit_normal)

    n_draws <- min(length(post_logit$alpha),
                   length(post_extreme$alpha),
                   length(post_normal$alpha))
    if (length(unique(c(length(post_logit$alpha),
                        length(post_extreme$alpha),
                        length(post_normal$alpha)))) > 1) {
      cat(sprintf(
        "[bayes_mixture_gamma] Note: draw counts differ across sub-models (logit=%d, extreme=%d, typical=%d) — using first %d draws from each\n",
        length(post_logit$alpha), length(post_extreme$alpha),
        length(post_normal$alpha), n_draws))
    }

    pred_draws      <- matrix(NA_real_, nrow = nrow(test), ncol = n_draws)
    p_extreme_draws <- matrix(NA_real_, nrow = nrow(test), ncol = n_draws)

    for (d in seq_len(n_draws)) {
      eta_logit_d <- post_logit$alpha[d] + X_test %*% post_logit$beta[d, ]
      p_ext_d     <- plogis(eta_logit_d)

      mu_ext_d  <- exp(post_extreme$alpha[d] + X_test %*% post_extreme$beta[d, ])
      mu_norm_d <- exp(post_normal$alpha[d]  + X_test %*% post_normal$beta[d, ])

      pred_draws[, d]      <- p_ext_d * mu_ext_d + (1 - p_ext_d) * mu_norm_d
      p_extreme_draws[, d] <- p_ext_d
    }

    p_hat  <- rowMeans(pred_draws)
    p_sd   <- apply(pred_draws, 1, sd)
    p_low  <- apply(pred_draws, 1, quantile, 0.025)
    p_high <- apply(pred_draws, 1, quantile, 0.975)

    extra$pred_sd        <- p_sd
    extra$pred_low        <- p_low
    extra$pred_high        <- p_high
    extra$p_extreme_mean  <- rowMeans(p_extreme_draws)
  }

  # ══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
  # Shared: metrics and output
  # ══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════

  metrics <- compute_burned_metrics(y_test, p_hat,
                                     n_boot = n_boot, seed = seed)

  cat(sprintf("[%s] nRMSE    : %.4f (%.4f, %.4f)\n",
              method, metrics$nrmse,   metrics$nrmse_ci[1],   metrics$nrmse_ci[2]))
  cat(sprintf("[%s] Pearson r: %.4f (%.4f, %.4f)\n",
              method, metrics$cor,     metrics$cor_ci[1],     metrics$cor_ci[2]))
  cat(sprintf("[%s] Spearman : %.4f (%.4f, %.4f)\n",
              method, metrics$spearman,metrics$spear_ci[1],   metrics$spear_ci[2]))
  cat(sprintf("[%s] R²       : %.4f (%.4f, %.4f)\n",
              method, metrics$r2,      metrics$r2_ci[1],      metrics$r2_ci[2]))
  cat(sprintf("[%s] MAE (km²): %.2f  (%.2f, %.2f)\n",
              method, metrics$mae,     metrics$mae_ci[1],     metrics$mae_ci[2]))
  cat(sprintf("[%s] Log corr : %.4f (%.4f, %.4f)\n",
              method, metrics$log_cor, metrics$log_cor_ci[1], metrics$log_cor_ci[2]))

  # Prediction data frame
  pred_df <- data.frame(
    lat                   = test$lat,
    lon                   = test$lon,
    year                  = test$year,
    month                 = test$month,
    burned_area_km2_total = y_test,
    burned_area_pred      = p_hat,
    residual              = y_test - p_hat,
    log_residual          = log(y_test + 1) - log(p_hat + 1)
  )

  # Add posterior uncertainty columns for Bayesian models
  if (!is.null(extra$pred_sd)) {
    pred_df$pred_sd   <- extra$pred_sd
    pred_df$pred_low  <- extra$pred_low
    pred_df$pred_high <- extra$pred_high
  }

  # Add extreme-probability column for the mixture model
  if (!is.null(extra$p_extreme_mean)) {
    pred_df$p_extreme <- extra$p_extreme_mean
  }

  c(
    list(
      method      = method,
      predictors  = predictors,
      outcome     = outcome,
      fit         = fit,
      coef_table  = coef_table,
      predictions = pred_df,
      metrics     = metrics
    ),
    extra   # appends aic, dispersion, loo, max_rhat, compiled_model, etc.
  )
}

# ── Convenience: compare metrics across fitted models ─────────────────────────

compare_burned_models <- function(model_list) {
  do.call(rbind, lapply(model_list, function(m) {
    mt <- m$metrics
    data.frame(
      method       = m$method,
      predictors   = paste(m$predictors, collapse = ", "),
      nrmse        = mt$nrmse,
      nrmse_low    = mt$nrmse_ci[1],
      nrmse_high   = mt$nrmse_ci[2],
      cor          = mt$cor,
      cor_low      = mt$cor_ci[1],
      cor_high     = mt$cor_ci[2],
      spearman     = mt$spearman,
      spear_low    = mt$spear_ci[1],
      spear_high   = mt$spear_ci[2],
      r2           = mt$r2,
      r2_low       = mt$r2_ci[1],
      r2_high      = mt$r2_ci[2],
      mae          = mt$mae,
      mae_low      = mt$mae_ci[1],
      mae_high     = mt$mae_ci[2],
      log_cor      = mt$log_cor,
      log_cor_low  = mt$log_cor_ci[1],
      log_cor_high = mt$log_cor_ci[2],
      row.names    = NULL
    )
  }))
}
```


Mixture model with input variable options, for testing different predictors for the calssifier, gamma extreme, and typical models
```{r}
##############################################################################
#
# fit_mixture_gamma_custom()
#
# Bayesian mixture burned-area model: logistic classifier (extreme vs typical)
# + separate Gamma magnitude models for extreme and typical fires — but unlike
# fit_burned_area_model()'s "bayes_mixture_gamma" method, each of the three
# sub-models can use its OWN predictor set, chosen for what that sub-model is
# actually trying to answer (e.g. classification signal vs. within-extreme
# magnitude signal, which can be quite different).
#
##############################################################################

options(mc.cores = parallel::detectCores())
rstan_options(auto_write = TRUE)

# ── Metrics helper (identical to compute_burned_metrics in your original) ───

compute_burned_metrics <- function(y_true, y_pred, n_boot = 1000, seed = 123) {
  rmse_val  <- sqrt(mean((y_pred - y_true)^2))
  nrmse_val <- rmse_val / mean(y_true)
  cor_val   <- cor(y_pred,  y_true)
  spear_val <- cor(y_pred,  y_true, method = "spearman")
  r2_val    <- 1 - sum((y_true - y_pred)^2) / sum((y_true - mean(y_true))^2)
  mae_val   <- mean(abs(y_pred - y_true))
  log_cor_val   <- cor(log(y_pred + 1), log(y_true + 1))
  log_rmse_val  <- sqrt(mean((log(y_pred + 1) - log(y_true + 1))^2))

  set.seed(seed)
  n        <- length(y_true)
  boot_mat <- matrix(
    NA_real_, nrow = n_boot, ncol = 7,
    dimnames = list(NULL, c("nrmse","cor","spear","r2","mae","log_cor","log_rmse"))
  )
  for (b in seq_len(n_boot)) {
    idx  <- sample.int(n, n, replace = TRUE)
    y_t  <- y_true[idx]; y_p  <- y_pred[idx]
    boot_mat[b, "nrmse"]    <- sqrt(mean((y_p - y_t)^2)) / mean(y_t)
    boot_mat[b, "cor"]      <- tryCatch(cor(y_p, y_t), error = function(e) NA_real_)
    boot_mat[b, "spear"]    <- tryCatch(cor(y_p, y_t, method = "spearman"), error = function(e) NA_real_)
    boot_mat[b, "r2"]       <- 1 - sum((y_t - y_p)^2) / sum((y_t - mean(y_t))^2)
    boot_mat[b, "mae"]      <- mean(abs(y_p - y_t))
    boot_mat[b, "log_cor"]  <- tryCatch(cor(log(y_p + 1), log(y_t + 1)), error = function(e) NA_real_)
    boot_mat[b, "log_rmse"] <- sqrt(mean((log(y_p + 1) - log(y_t + 1))^2))
  }
  qfun <- function(x) quantile(x[is.finite(x)], probs = c(0.025, 0.975), na.rm = TRUE)

  list(
    nrmse = nrmse_val, nrmse_ci = qfun(boot_mat[, "nrmse"]),
    cor = cor_val, cor_ci = qfun(boot_mat[, "cor"]),
    spearman = spear_val, spear_ci = qfun(boot_mat[, "spear"]),
    r2 = r2_val, r2_ci = qfun(boot_mat[, "r2"]),
    mae = mae_val, mae_ci = qfun(boot_mat[, "mae"]),
    log_cor = log_cor_val, log_cor_ci = qfun(boot_mat[, "log_cor"]),
    log_rmse = log_rmse_val, log_rmse_ci = qfun(boot_mat[, "log_rmse"])
  )
}

# ── Stan model code (identical to your original) ─────────────────────────────

.stan_gamma <- "
data {
  int<lower=1> N;
  int<lower=1> K;
  matrix[N, K] X;
  vector<lower=0>[N] y;
  real<lower=0> sigma_beta;
  real<lower=0> sigma_alpha;
}
parameters {
  real alpha;
  vector[K] beta;
  real<lower=0> phi;
}
model {
  alpha ~ normal(0, sigma_alpha);
  beta  ~ normal(0, sigma_beta);
  phi   ~ exponential(0.1);
  for (n in 1:N) {
    real mu_n = exp(alpha + dot_product(X[n], beta));
    y[n] ~ gamma(phi, phi / mu_n);
  }
}
generated quantities {
  vector[N] log_lik;
  vector[N] y_pred;
  for (n in 1:N) {
    real mu_n  = exp(alpha + dot_product(X[n], beta));
    log_lik[n] = gamma_lpdf(y[n] | phi, phi / mu_n);
    y_pred[n]  = mu_n;
  }
}"

.stan_bernoulli <- "
data {
  int<lower=1> N;
  int<lower=1> K;
  matrix[N, K] X;
  int<lower=0,upper=1> y[N];
  real<lower=0> sigma_beta;
  real<lower=0> sigma_alpha;
}
parameters {
  real alpha;
  vector[K] beta;
}
model {
  alpha ~ normal(0, sigma_alpha);
  beta  ~ normal(0, sigma_beta);
  y ~ bernoulli_logit(alpha + X * beta);
}
generated quantities {
  vector[N] log_lik;
  for (n in 1:N)
    log_lik[n] = bernoulli_logit_lpmf(y[n] | alpha + dot_product(X[n], beta));
}"

# ── Main function ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────

fit_mixture_gamma_custom <- function(train,
                                      test,
                                      preds_classifier,
                                      preds_extreme,
                                      preds_typical,
                                      outcome           = "burned_area_km2_total",
                                      extreme_quantile  = 0.95,
                                      sigma_beta        = 1,
                                      sigma_alpha       = 5,
                                      iter              = 2000,
                                      chains            = 4,
                                      seed              = 123,
                                      n_boot            = 1000,
                                      adapt_delta       = 0.95,
                                      compiled_model    = NULL) {
  # ── Args ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
  # preds_classifier : predictor names for the extreme-vs-typical classifier
  # preds_extreme     : predictor names for the extreme-fire Gamma model
  # preds_typical     : predictor names for the typical-fire Gamma model
  #                     (all three may differ in length and content)
  # compiled_model    : optional pre-compiled list(logistic = ..., gamma = ...)
  #                     to skip recompilation across repeated calls

  if (any(train[[outcome]] <= 0)) {
    stop(sprintf("All values of '%s' must be > 0. Found %d non-positive values.",
                 outcome, sum(train[[outcome]] <= 0)))
  }

  y_train <- train[[outcome]]
  y_test  <- test[[outcome]]

  threshold <- quantile(y_train, extreme_quantile)
  cat(sprintf("[mixture_custom] Extreme threshold (%.0fth pct of train): %.2f km²\n",
              extreme_quantile * 100, threshold))

  is_extreme_train <- as.integer(y_train >= threshold)
  cat(sprintf("[mixture_custom] Extreme fires in train: %d / %d (%.1f%%)\n",
              sum(is_extreme_train), length(is_extreme_train), 100 * mean(is_extreme_train)))

  fm_classifier <- as.formula(paste("~", paste(preds_classifier, collapse = " + "), "- 1"))
  fm_extreme    <- as.formula(paste("~", paste(preds_extreme,    collapse = " + "), "- 1"))
  fm_typical    <- as.formula(paste("~", paste(preds_typical,    collapse = " + "), "- 1"))

  # ── Compile (or reuse) Stan models ───────────────────────────────────────
  if (is.null(compiled_model) || is.null(compiled_model$logistic)) {
    cat("[mixture_custom] Compiling classification (logistic) Stan model...\n")
    sm_logit <- stan_model(model_code = .stan_bernoulli, model_name = "mixture_custom_logit")
  } else {
    sm_logit <- compiled_model$logistic
  }
  if (is.null(compiled_model) || is.null(compiled_model$gamma)) {
    cat("[mixture_custom] Compiling magnitude (Gamma) Stan model...\n")
    sm_gamma <- stan_model(model_code = .stan_gamma, model_name = "mixture_custom_gamma")
  } else {
    sm_gamma <- compiled_model$gamma
  }

  # ── 1. Classifier ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
  X_train_clf <- model.matrix(fm_classifier, data = train)
  X_test_clf  <- model.matrix(fm_classifier, data = test)

  stan_data_logit <- list(
    N = nrow(train), K = ncol(X_train_clf), X = X_train_clf,
    y = is_extreme_train, sigma_beta = sigma_beta, sigma_alpha = sigma_alpha
  )

  cat("[mixture_custom] Sampling classification model...\n")
  fit_logit <- sampling(sm_logit, data = stan_data_logit,
                         iter = iter, chains = chains, seed = seed,
                         control = list(adapt_delta = adapt_delta), refresh = 200)

  div_logit  <- rstan::get_num_divergent(fit_logit)
  rhat_logit <- max(summary(fit_logit)$summary[, "Rhat"], na.rm = TRUE)
  cat(sprintf("[mixture_custom] Classifier: divergences=%d, max R-hat=%.4f %s\n",
              div_logit, rhat_logit, ifelse(rhat_logit > 1.01 || div_logit > 0, "\u26a0", "\u2713")))

  # ── 2. Extreme-fire magnitude model ──────────────────────────────────────
  train_extreme <- train[is_extreme_train == 1, , drop = FALSE]
  y_extreme     <- y_train[is_extreme_train == 1]
  X_extreme     <- model.matrix(fm_extreme, data = train_extreme)
  X_test_ext    <- model.matrix(fm_extreme, data = test)

  stan_data_extreme <- list(
    N = nrow(train_extreme), K = ncol(X_extreme), X = X_extreme, y = y_extreme,
    sigma_beta = sigma_beta, sigma_alpha = sigma_alpha
  )

  cat(sprintf("[mixture_custom] Sampling extreme-fire magnitude model (N=%d, K=%d)...\n",
              nrow(train_extreme), ncol(X_extreme)))
  fit_extreme <- sampling(sm_gamma, data = stan_data_extreme,
                           iter = iter, chains = chains, seed = seed,
                           control = list(adapt_delta = adapt_delta), refresh = 200)

  div_extreme  <- rstan::get_num_divergent(fit_extreme)
  rhat_extreme <- max(summary(fit_extreme)$summary[, "Rhat"], na.rm = TRUE)
  cat(sprintf("[mixture_custom] Extreme model: divergences=%d, max R-hat=%.4f %s\n",
              div_extreme, rhat_extreme, ifelse(rhat_extreme > 1.01 || div_extreme > 0, "\u26a0", "\u2713")))

  # ── 3. Typical-fire magnitude model ──────────────────────────────────────
  train_normal <- train[is_extreme_train == 0, , drop = FALSE]
  y_normal     <- y_train[is_extreme_train == 0]
  X_normal     <- model.matrix(fm_typical, data = train_normal)
  X_test_typ   <- model.matrix(fm_typical, data = test)

  stan_data_normal <- list(
    N = nrow(train_normal), K = ncol(X_normal), X = X_normal, y = y_normal,
    sigma_beta = sigma_beta, sigma_alpha = sigma_alpha
  )

  cat(sprintf("[mixture_custom] Sampling typical-fire magnitude model (N=%d, K=%d)...\n",
              nrow(train_normal), ncol(X_normal)))
  fit_normal <- sampling(sm_gamma, data = stan_data_normal,
                          iter = iter, chains = chains, seed = seed,
                          control = list(adapt_delta = adapt_delta), refresh = 200)

  div_normal  <- rstan::get_num_divergent(fit_normal)
  rhat_normal <- max(summary(fit_normal)$summary[, "Rhat"], na.rm = TRUE)
  cat(sprintf("[mixture_custom] Typical model: divergences=%d, max R-hat=%.4f %s\n",
              div_normal, rhat_normal, ifelse(rhat_normal > 1.01 || div_normal > 0, "\u26a0", "\u2713")))

  max_rhat  <- max(rhat_logit, rhat_extreme, rhat_normal, na.rm = TRUE)
  total_div <- div_logit + div_extreme + div_normal

  if (total_div > 0 || max_rhat > 1.05) {
    warning(sprintf(
      "One or more sub-models did not converge cleanly (total divergences: %d, max R-hat: %.4f). Inspect before trusting predictions.",
      total_div, max_rhat))
  }

  # ── Posterior summaries ──────────────────────────────────────────────────
  summ_logit   <- summary(fit_logit,   pars = c("alpha", "beta"))$summary
  summ_extreme <- summary(fit_extreme, pars = c("alpha", "beta", "phi"))$summary
  summ_normal  <- summary(fit_normal,  pars = c("alpha", "beta", "phi"))$summary

  coef_table <- rbind(
    transform(as.data.frame(summ_logit),
              variable  = c("alpha", paste0("beta_", colnames(X_train_clf))),
              component = "classification"),
    transform(as.data.frame(summ_extreme),
              variable  = c("alpha", paste0("beta_", colnames(X_extreme)), "phi"),
              component = "magnitude_extreme"),
    transform(as.data.frame(summ_normal),
              variable  = c("alpha", paste0("beta_", colnames(X_normal)), "phi"),
              component = "magnitude_typical")
  )
  rownames(coef_table) <- NULL

  # ── Predictions on test set: three separate design matrices, one blend ──
  post_logit   <- rstan::extract(fit_logit)
  post_extreme <- rstan::extract(fit_extreme)
  post_normal  <- rstan::extract(fit_normal)

  n_draws <- min(length(post_logit$alpha), length(post_extreme$alpha), length(post_normal$alpha))

  pred_draws      <- matrix(NA_real_, nrow = nrow(test), ncol = n_draws)
  p_extreme_draws <- matrix(NA_real_, nrow = nrow(test), ncol = n_draws)

  for (d in seq_len(n_draws)) {
    p_ext_d <- plogis(post_logit$alpha[d] + X_test_clf %*% post_logit$beta[d, ])

    mu_ext_d  <- exp(post_extreme$alpha[d] + X_test_ext %*% post_extreme$beta[d, ])
    mu_norm_d <- exp(post_normal$alpha[d]  + X_test_typ %*% post_normal$beta[d, ])

    pred_draws[, d]      <- p_ext_d * mu_ext_d + (1 - p_ext_d) * mu_norm_d
    p_extreme_draws[, d] <- p_ext_d
  }

  p_hat  <- apply(pred_draws, 1, median, na.rm = TRUE)   # median: robust to any residual unstable draws
  p_sd   <- apply(pred_draws, 1, sd,    na.rm = TRUE)
  p_low  <- apply(pred_draws, 1, quantile, 0.025, na.rm = TRUE)
  p_high <- apply(pred_draws, 1, quantile, 0.975, na.rm = TRUE)
  p_extreme_mean <- apply(p_extreme_draws, 1, median, na.rm = TRUE)

  # ── Metrics ───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
  metrics <- compute_burned_metrics(y_test, p_hat, n_boot = n_boot, seed = seed)

  cat(sprintf("[mixture_custom] nRMSE    : %.4f (%.4f, %.4f)\n",
              metrics$nrmse, metrics$nrmse_ci[1], metrics$nrmse_ci[2]))
  cat(sprintf("[mixture_custom] Pearson r: %.4f (%.4f, %.4f)\n",
              metrics$cor, metrics$cor_ci[1], metrics$cor_ci[2]))
  cat(sprintf("[mixture_custom] Spearman : %.4f (%.4f, %.4f)\n",
              metrics$spearman, metrics$spear_ci[1], metrics$spear_ci[2]))
  cat(sprintf("[mixture_custom] R\u00b2       : %.4f (%.4f, %.4f)\n",
              metrics$r2, metrics$r2_ci[1], metrics$r2_ci[2]))
  cat(sprintf("[mixture_custom] MAE (km\u00b2): %.2f  (%.2f, %.2f)\n",
              metrics$mae, metrics$mae_ci[1], metrics$mae_ci[2]))
  cat(sprintf("[mixture_custom] Log corr : %.4f (%.4f, %.4f)\n",
              metrics$log_cor, metrics$log_cor_ci[1], metrics$log_cor_ci[2]))

  pred_df <- data.frame(
    lat = test$lat, lon = test$lon, year = test$year, month = test$month,
    burned_area_km2_total = y_test,
    burned_area_pred      = p_hat,
    residual              = y_test - p_hat,
    log_residual          = log(y_test + 1) - log(p_hat + 1),
    pred_sd    = p_sd,
    pred_low   = p_low,
    pred_high  = p_high,
    p_extreme  = p_extreme_mean
  )

  list(
    method            = "mixture_gamma_custom",
    preds_classifier  = preds_classifier,
    preds_extreme     = preds_extreme,
    preds_typical     = preds_typical,
    outcome           = outcome,
    threshold         = threshold,
    extreme_quantile  = extreme_quantile,
    fit_logit         = fit_logit,
    fit_extreme       = fit_extreme,
    fit_normal        = fit_normal,
    coef_table        = coef_table,
    predictions       = pred_df,
    metrics           = metrics,
    max_rhat          = max_rhat,
    max_rhat_logit    = rhat_logit,
    max_rhat_extreme  = rhat_extreme,
    max_rhat_normal   = rhat_normal,
    total_divergences = total_div,
    div_logit         = div_logit,
    div_extreme       = div_extreme,
    div_normal        = div_normal,
    compiled_model    = list(logistic = sm_logit, gamma = sm_gamma)
  )
}
```

Previous models sample values from zero to infinity for both the extreme and typical fires. However, the extreme gamma model is only trained on burned areas above a threshold. To better constrain the extreme gamma model, a truncated gamma model is applied when generating predictions from the already-fitted extreme-fire model.

instead of using the Gamma's raw, untruncated mean when blending the extreme and typical predictions together, the truncated version computes the mean of the same Gamma distribution conditional on being above the threshold — i.e., "given that this value is at least as large as the extreme cutoff, what's its expected size?" This uses a standard closed-form identity for truncated Gamma distributions, built from the same shape and rate parameters the model already estimated — no new fitting, just a different way of summarizing the already-fitted distribution. Since conditioning on "above threshold" always excludes the low end, this corrected mean is always somewhat larger than the raw untruncated mean would have been.

classifier fit → same; both Gamma models fit → same; only the number pulled out of the extreme-fire Gamma at prediction time changes, from "the raw mean" to "the mean given it's actually large enough to count as extreme." Everything downstream (blending with the typical-fire prediction, computing performance metrics) uses that corrected number in exactly the same way as before.

# =============================================================================
# Truncated-Gamma mean, left-truncated at `threshold`.
# Standard identity for E[Y | Y > threshold], Y ~ Gamma(shape, rate):
#   E[Y | Y > tau] = (shape/rate) * [1 - pgamma(tau, shape+1, rate)]
#                                   -----------------------------------
#                                   [1 - pgamma(tau, shape,   rate)]
# The untruncated Gamma mean (shape/rate) is recovered as threshold -> 0.
# =============================================================================
```{r}
truncated_gamma_mean <- function(shape, rate, threshold) {
  numerator   <- 1 - pgamma(threshold, shape = shape + 1, rate = rate)
  denominator <- 1 - pgamma(threshold, shape = shape,     rate = rate)
  # Guard against numerical underflow when the denominator is ~0 (a draw
  # whose fitted distribution puts essentially no mass above threshold at
  # all) -- fall back to the untruncated mean rather than producing NaN/Inf
  ifelse(denominator > 1e-10, (shape / rate) * (numerator / denominator), shape / rate)
}

fit_mixture_gamma_custom_truncated <- function(train,
                                                test,
                                                preds_classifier,
                                                preds_extreme,
                                                preds_typical,
                                                outcome           = "burned_area_km2_total",
                                                extreme_quantile  = 0.95,
                                                sigma_beta        = 1,
                                                sigma_alpha       = 5,
                                                iter              = 2000,
                                                chains            = 4,
                                                seed              = 123,
                                                n_boot            = 1000,
                                                adapt_delta       = 0.95,
                                                compiled_model    = NULL) {
  # Identical to fit_mixture_gamma_custom() in every respect EXCEPT the
  # extreme component's predicted mean, which is corrected for left-
  # truncation at `threshold` (see truncated_gamma_mean() above). The
  # classifier and both Gamma sub-models are fit EXACTLY as before -- this
  # does not modify the likelihood used during fitting (that would require
  # editing .stan_gamma's Stan code directly, which this function does not
  # have access to); it corrects the MEAN used when generating predictions,
  # so that "a fire classified extreme" can no longer be represented by an
  # implausibly small predicted magnitude.

  if (any(train[[outcome]] <= 0)) {
    stop(sprintf("All values of '%s' must be > 0. Found %d non-positive values.",
                 outcome, sum(train[[outcome]] <= 0)))
  }

  y_train <- train[[outcome]]
  y_test  <- test[[outcome]]

  threshold <- quantile(y_train, extreme_quantile)
  cat(sprintf("[mixture_custom_truncated] Extreme threshold (%.0fth pct of train): %.2f km\u00b2\n",
              extreme_quantile * 100, threshold))

  is_extreme_train <- as.integer(y_train >= threshold)
  cat(sprintf("[mixture_custom_truncated] Extreme fires in train: %d / %d (%.1f%%)\n",
              sum(is_extreme_train), length(is_extreme_train), 100 * mean(is_extreme_train)))

  fm_classifier <- as.formula(paste("~", paste(preds_classifier, collapse = " + "), "- 1"))
  fm_extreme    <- as.formula(paste("~", paste(preds_extreme,    collapse = " + "), "- 1"))
  fm_typical    <- as.formula(paste("~", paste(preds_typical,    collapse = " + "), "- 1"))

  # ── Compile (or reuse) Stan models -- UNCHANGED from fit_mixture_gamma_custom() ──
  if (is.null(compiled_model) || is.null(compiled_model$logistic)) {
    cat("[mixture_custom_truncated] Compiling classification (logistic) Stan model...\n")
    sm_logit <- stan_model(model_code = .stan_bernoulli, model_name = "mixture_custom_truncated_logit")
  } else {
    sm_logit <- compiled_model$logistic
  }
  if (is.null(compiled_model) || is.null(compiled_model$gamma)) {
    cat("[mixture_custom_truncated] Compiling magnitude (Gamma) Stan model...\n")
    sm_gamma <- stan_model(model_code = .stan_gamma, model_name = "mixture_custom_truncated_gamma")
  } else {
    sm_gamma <- compiled_model$gamma
  }

  # ── 1. Classifier -- UNCHANGED ───────────────────────────────────────────
  X_train_clf <- model.matrix(fm_classifier, data = train)
  X_test_clf  <- model.matrix(fm_classifier, data = test)

  stan_data_logit <- list(
    N = nrow(train), K = ncol(X_train_clf), X = X_train_clf,
    y = is_extreme_train, sigma_beta = sigma_beta, sigma_alpha = sigma_alpha
  )

  cat("[mixture_custom_truncated] Sampling classification model...\n")
  fit_logit <- sampling(sm_logit, data = stan_data_logit,
                         iter = iter, chains = chains, seed = seed,
                         control = list(adapt_delta = adapt_delta), refresh = 200)

  div_logit  <- rstan::get_num_divergent(fit_logit)
  rhat_logit <- max(summary(fit_logit)$summary[, "Rhat"], na.rm = TRUE)
  cat(sprintf("[mixture_custom_truncated] Classifier: divergences=%d, max R-hat=%.4f %s\n",
              div_logit, rhat_logit, ifelse(rhat_logit > 1.01 || div_logit > 0, "\u26a0", "\u2713")))

  # ── 2. Extreme-fire magnitude model -- fitting UNCHANGED ────────────────
  train_extreme <- train[is_extreme_train == 1, , drop = FALSE]
  y_extreme     <- y_train[is_extreme_train == 1]
  X_extreme     <- model.matrix(fm_extreme, data = train_extreme)
  X_test_ext    <- model.matrix(fm_extreme, data = test)

  stan_data_extreme <- list(
    N = nrow(train_extreme), K = ncol(X_extreme), X = X_extreme, y = y_extreme,
    sigma_beta = sigma_beta, sigma_alpha = sigma_alpha
  )

  cat(sprintf("[mixture_custom_truncated] Sampling extreme-fire magnitude model (N=%d, K=%d)...\n",
              nrow(train_extreme), ncol(X_extreme)))
  fit_extreme <- sampling(sm_gamma, data = stan_data_extreme,
                           iter = iter, chains = chains, seed = seed,
                           control = list(adapt_delta = adapt_delta), refresh = 200)

  div_extreme  <- rstan::get_num_divergent(fit_extreme)
  rhat_extreme <- max(summary(fit_extreme)$summary[, "Rhat"], na.rm = TRUE)
  cat(sprintf("[mixture_custom_truncated] Extreme model: divergences=%d, max R-hat=%.4f %s\n",
              div_extreme, rhat_extreme, ifelse(rhat_extreme > 1.01 || div_extreme > 0, "\u26a0", "\u2713")))

  # ── 3. Typical-fire magnitude model -- UNCHANGED ─────────────────────────
  train_normal <- train[is_extreme_train == 0, , drop = FALSE]
  y_normal     <- y_train[is_extreme_train == 0]
  X_normal     <- model.matrix(fm_typical, data = train_normal)
  X_test_typ   <- model.matrix(fm_typical, data = test)

  stan_data_normal <- list(
    N = nrow(train_normal), K = ncol(X_normal), X = X_normal, y = y_normal,
    sigma_beta = sigma_beta, sigma_alpha = sigma_alpha
  )

  cat(sprintf("[mixture_custom_truncated] Sampling typical-fire magnitude model (N=%d, K=%d)...\n",
              nrow(train_normal), ncol(X_normal)))
  fit_normal <- sampling(sm_gamma, data = stan_data_normal,
                          iter = iter, chains = chains, seed = seed,
                          control = list(adapt_delta = adapt_delta), refresh = 200)

  div_normal  <- rstan::get_num_divergent(fit_normal)
  rhat_normal <- max(summary(fit_normal)$summary[, "Rhat"], na.rm = TRUE)
  cat(sprintf("[mixture_custom_truncated] Typical model: divergences=%d, max R-hat=%.4f %s\n",
              div_normal, rhat_normal, ifelse(rhat_normal > 1.01 || div_normal > 0, "\u26a0", "\u2713")))

  max_rhat  <- max(rhat_logit, rhat_extreme, rhat_normal, na.rm = TRUE)
  total_div <- div_logit + div_extreme + div_normal

  if (total_div > 0 || max_rhat > 1.05) {
    warning(sprintf(
      "One or more sub-models did not converge cleanly (total divergences: %d, max R-hat: %.4f). Inspect before trusting predictions.",
      total_div, max_rhat))
  }

  # ── Posterior summaries -- UNCHANGED ─────────────────────────────────────
  summ_logit   <- summary(fit_logit,   pars = c("alpha", "beta"))$summary
  summ_extreme <- summary(fit_extreme, pars = c("alpha", "beta", "phi"))$summary
  summ_normal  <- summary(fit_normal,  pars = c("alpha", "beta", "phi"))$summary

  coef_table <- rbind(
    transform(as.data.frame(summ_logit),
              variable  = c("alpha", paste0("beta_", colnames(X_train_clf))),
              component = "classification"),
    transform(as.data.frame(summ_extreme),
              variable  = c("alpha", paste0("beta_", colnames(X_extreme)), "phi"),
              component = "magnitude_extreme"),
    transform(as.data.frame(summ_normal),
              variable  = c("alpha", paste0("beta_", colnames(X_normal)), "phi"),
              component = "magnitude_typical")
  )
  rownames(coef_table) <- NULL

  # ── Predictions: SAME structure as fit_mixture_gamma_custom(), but the
  # extreme component's mean is now the LEFT-TRUNCATED Gamma mean (at
  # `threshold`) rather than the raw untruncated exp(alpha + X*beta) --
  # this is the one substantive change in this whole function ─────────────
  post_logit   <- rstan::extract(fit_logit)
  post_extreme <- rstan::extract(fit_extreme)
  post_normal  <- rstan::extract(fit_normal)

  n_draws <- min(length(post_logit$alpha), length(post_extreme$alpha), length(post_normal$alpha))

  pred_draws      <- matrix(NA_real_, nrow = nrow(test), ncol = n_draws)
  p_extreme_draws <- matrix(NA_real_, nrow = nrow(test), ncol = n_draws)

  for (d in seq_len(n_draws)) {
    p_ext_d <- plogis(post_logit$alpha[d] + X_test_clf %*% post_logit$beta[d, ])

    mu_ext_raw_d <- as.numeric(exp(post_extreme$alpha[d] + X_test_ext %*% post_extreme$beta[d, ]))
    phi_ext_d    <- post_extreme$phi[d]
    rate_ext_d   <- phi_ext_d / mu_ext_raw_d

    # THE FIX: truncated mean, using this draw's own shape (phi) and rate,
    # in place of the untruncated mu_ext_raw_d used previously
    mu_ext_d <- truncated_gamma_mean(shape = phi_ext_d, rate = rate_ext_d, threshold = threshold)

    mu_norm_d <- exp(post_normal$alpha[d] + X_test_typ %*% post_normal$beta[d, ])

    pred_draws[, d]      <- p_ext_d * mu_ext_d + (1 - p_ext_d) * mu_norm_d
    p_extreme_draws[, d] <- p_ext_d
  }

  p_hat  <- apply(pred_draws, 1, median, na.rm = TRUE)
  p_sd   <- apply(pred_draws, 1, sd,    na.rm = TRUE)
  p_low  <- apply(pred_draws, 1, quantile, 0.025, na.rm = TRUE)
  p_high <- apply(pred_draws, 1, quantile, 0.975, na.rm = TRUE)
  p_extreme_mean <- apply(p_extreme_draws, 1, median, na.rm = TRUE)

  # ── Metrics -- SAME function as every other model, for direct comparability ──
  metrics <- compute_burned_metrics(y_test, p_hat, n_boot = n_boot, seed = seed)

  cat(sprintf("[mixture_custom_truncated] nRMSE    : %.4f (%.4f, %.4f)\n",
              metrics$nrmse, metrics$nrmse_ci[1], metrics$nrmse_ci[2]))
  cat(sprintf("[mixture_custom_truncated] Pearson r: %.4f (%.4f, %.4f)\n",
              metrics$cor, metrics$cor_ci[1], metrics$cor_ci[2]))
  cat(sprintf("[mixture_custom_truncated] Spearman : %.4f (%.4f, %.4f)\n",
              metrics$spearman, metrics$spearman_ci[1], metrics$spearman_ci[2]))

  pred_df <- tibble(
    lat = test$lat, lon = test$lon, year = test$year, month = test$month,
    burned_area_km2_total = y_test,
    burned_area_pred      = p_hat,
    residual              = y_test - p_hat,
    log_residual          = log(y_test + 1) - log(p_hat + 1),
    pred_sd    = p_sd,
    pred_low   = p_low,
    pred_high  = p_high,
    p_extreme  = p_extreme_mean
  )

  list(
    method            = "mixture_gamma_custom_truncated",
    preds_classifier  = preds_classifier,
    preds_extreme     = preds_extreme,
    preds_typical     = preds_typical,
    outcome           = outcome,
    threshold         = threshold,
    extreme_quantile  = extreme_quantile,
    fit_logit         = fit_logit,
    fit_extreme       = fit_extreme,
    fit_normal        = fit_normal,
    coef_table        = coef_table,
    predictions       = pred_df,
    metrics           = metrics,
    max_rhat          = max_rhat,
    max_rhat_logit    = rhat_logit,
    max_rhat_extreme  = rhat_extreme,
    max_rhat_normal   = rhat_normal,
    total_divergences = total_div,
    div_logit         = div_logit,
    div_extreme       = div_extreme,
    div_normal        = div_normal,
    compiled_model    = list(logistic = sm_logit, gamma = sm_gamma)
  )
}
```

    May be worth again including RH (-0.25135813) since its influece on burned area is opposite to fire count.

preds_typical    <- c("urban_proximity_binary", "vpd", "rh")  # tair, tair_2m replaced by vpd

m19_mixture_custom_truncated <- run_or_load_model(
  file.path(rds_root, "m19_bayes_mixture_custom_truncated.rds"),
  fit_mixture_gamma_custom_truncated(
    train, test,
    preds_classifier = preds_classifier,
    preds_extreme    = preds_extreme,
    preds_typical    = preds_typical,
    chains = 4
))
