Try interaction terms that were explored at the start of the script:
```{r}
# =============================================================================
# fit_mixture_gamma_formula(): same three-component structure as
# fit_mixture_gamma_custom()/_truncated(), but takes FULL FORMULA OBJECTS
# for each component instead of plain predictor-name vectors -- necessary
# to support interaction terms (rh * U, wind * rh, etc.), which a simple
# "paste(preds, collapse = '+')" approach cannot express.
#
# Truncation is deliberately NOT a fitting-time argument: it only affects
# how predictions are SAMPLED from the already-fitted extreme-fire Gamma
# (see sample_mixture_predictions()'s truncate_extreme argument), not how
# the classifier/extreme/typical models are estimated. Nothing about the
# posterior itself changes based on whether you later sample truncated
# or untruncated.
# =============================================================================
fit_mixture_gamma_formula <- function(train,
                                       test,
                                       formula_classifier,   # one-sided, e.g. ~ rh * urban_proximity_binary + rh * U + rh * vpd + tair_5y
                                       formula_extreme,      # one-sided, e.g. ~ wind * rh + C + U
                                       formula_typical,      # one-sided, e.g. ~ urban_proximity_binary + rh + precip_5y + precip_3m + vpd + tair_2m
                                       outcome           = "burned_area_km2_total",
                                       extreme_quantile  = 0.95,
                                       sigma_beta        = 1,
                                       sigma_alpha       = 5,
                                       iter              = 2000,
                                       chains            = 4,
                                       seed              = 123,
                                       n_boot            = 1000,
                                       adapt_delta       = 0.95,
                                       compiled_model    = NULL) {

  if (any(train[[outcome]] <= 0)) {
    stop(sprintf("All values of '%s' must be > 0. Found %d non-positive values.",
                 outcome, sum(train[[outcome]] <= 0)))
  }

  y_train <- train[[outcome]]
  y_test  <- test[[outcome]]

  threshold <- quantile(y_train, extreme_quantile)
  cat(sprintf("[mixture_formula] Extreme threshold (%.0fth pct of train): %.2f km\u00b2\n",
              extreme_quantile * 100, threshold))

  is_extreme_train <- as.integer(y_train >= threshold)
  cat(sprintf("[mixture_formula] Extreme fires in train: %d / %d (%.1f%%)\n",
              sum(is_extreme_train), length(is_extreme_train), 100 * mean(is_extreme_train)))

  # Suppress the intercept column in each design matrix (Stan estimates
  # alpha separately) -- append "- 1" to whatever formula was supplied,
  # rather than requiring the user to remember to write it themselves
  fm_classifier <- update(formula_classifier, ~ . - 1)
  fm_extreme    <- update(formula_extreme,    ~ . - 1)
  fm_typical    <- update(formula_typical,    ~ . - 1)

  # ── Compile (or reuse) Stan models ───────────────────────────────────────
  if (is.null(compiled_model) || is.null(compiled_model$logistic)) {
    cat("[mixture_formula] Compiling classification (logistic) Stan model...\n")
    sm_logit <- stan_model(model_code = .stan_bernoulli, model_name = "mixture_formula_logit")
  } else {
    sm_logit <- compiled_model$logistic
  }
  if (is.null(compiled_model) || is.null(compiled_model$gamma)) {
    cat("[mixture_formula] Compiling magnitude (Gamma) Stan model...\n")
    sm_gamma <- stan_model(model_code = .stan_gamma, model_name = "mixture_formula_gamma")
  } else {
    sm_gamma <- compiled_model$gamma
  }

  # ── 1. Classifier ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
  X_train_clf <- model.matrix(fm_classifier, data = train)
  X_test_clf  <- model.matrix(fm_classifier, data = test)

  stan_data_logit <- list(
    N = nrow(train), K = ncol(X_train_clf), X = X_train_clf,
    y = is_extreme_train, sigma_beta = sigma_beta, sigma_alpha = sigma_alpha
  )

  cat("[mixture_formula] Sampling classification model...\n")
  fit_logit <- sampling(sm_logit, data = stan_data_logit,
                         iter = iter, chains = chains, seed = seed,
                         control = list(adapt_delta = adapt_delta), refresh = 200)

  div_logit  <- rstan::get_num_divergent(fit_logit)
  rhat_logit <- max(summary(fit_logit)$summary[, "Rhat"], na.rm = TRUE)
  cat(sprintf("[mixture_formula] Classifier: divergences=%d, max R-hat=%.4f %s\n",
              div_logit, rhat_logit, ifelse(rhat_logit > 1.01 || div_logit > 0, "\u26a0", "\u2713")))

  # ── 2. Extreme-fire magnitude model ──────────────────────────────────────
  train_extreme <- train[is_extreme_train == 1, , drop = FALSE]
  y_extreme     <- y_train[is_extreme_train == 1]
  X_extreme     <- model.matrix(fm_extreme, data = train_extreme)
  X_test_ext    <- model.matrix(fm_extreme, data = test)

  stan_data_extreme <- list(
    N = nrow(train_extreme), K = ncol(X_extreme), X = X_extreme, y = y_extreme,
    sigma_beta = sigma_beta, sigma_alpha = sigma_alpha
  )

  cat(sprintf("[mixture_formula] Sampling extreme-fire magnitude model (N=%d, K=%d)...\n",
              nrow(train_extreme), ncol(X_extreme)))
  fit_extreme <- sampling(sm_gamma, data = stan_data_extreme,
                           iter = iter, chains = chains, seed = seed,
                           control = list(adapt_delta = adapt_delta), refresh = 200)

  div_extreme  <- rstan::get_num_divergent(fit_extreme)
  rhat_extreme <- max(summary(fit_extreme)$summary[, "Rhat"], na.rm = TRUE)
  cat(sprintf("[mixture_formula] Extreme model: divergences=%d, max R-hat=%.4f %s\n",
              div_extreme, rhat_extreme, ifelse(rhat_extreme > 1.01 || div_extreme > 0, "\u26a0", "\u2713")))

  # ── 3. Typical-fire magnitude model ──────────────────────────────────────
  train_normal <- train[is_extreme_train == 0, , drop = FALSE]
  y_normal     <- y_train[is_extreme_train == 0]
  X_normal     <- model.matrix(fm_typical, data = train_normal)
  X_test_typ   <- model.matrix(fm_typical, data = test)

  stan_data_normal <- list(
    N = nrow(train_normal), K = ncol(X_normal), X = X_normal, y = y_normal,
    sigma_beta = sigma_beta, sigma_alpha = sigma_alpha
  )

  cat(sprintf("[mixture_formula] Sampling typical-fire magnitude model (N=%d, K=%d)...\n",
              nrow(train_normal), ncol(X_normal)))
  fit_normal <- sampling(sm_gamma, data = stan_data_normal,
                          iter = iter, chains = chains, seed = seed,
                          control = list(adapt_delta = adapt_delta), refresh = 200)

  div_normal  <- rstan::get_num_divergent(fit_normal)
  rhat_normal <- max(summary(fit_normal)$summary[, "Rhat"], na.rm = TRUE)
  cat(sprintf("[mixture_formula] Typical model: divergences=%d, max R-hat=%.4f %s\n",
              div_normal, rhat_normal, ifelse(rhat_normal > 1.01 || div_normal > 0, "\u26a0", "\u2713")))

  max_rhat  <- max(rhat_logit, rhat_extreme, rhat_normal, na.rm = TRUE)
  total_div <- div_logit + div_extreme + div_normal

  if (total_div > 0 || max_rhat > 1.05) {
    warning(sprintf(
      "One or more sub-models did not converge cleanly (total divergences: %d, max R-hat: %.4f). Inspect before trusting predictions.",
      total_div, max_rhat))
  }

  # ── Posterior summaries -- column names now naturally include the
  # interaction terms (e.g. "rh:urban_proximity_binaryX"), since they come
  # straight from model.matrix()'s own naming, not a manually-pasted list ──
  summ_logit   <- summary(fit_logit,   pars = c("alpha", "beta"))$summary
  summ_extreme <- summary(fit_extreme, pars = c("alpha", "beta", "phi"))$summary
  summ_normal  <- summary(fit_normal,  pars = c("alpha", "beta", "phi"))$summary

  coef_table <- rbind(
    transform(as.data.frame(summ_logit),
              variable  = c("alpha", paste0("beta_", colnames(X_train_clf))),
              component = "classification"),
    transform(as.data.frame(summ_extreme),
              variable  = c("alpha", paste0("beta_", colnames(X_extreme)), "phi"),
              component = "magnitude_extreme"),
    transform(as.data.frame(summ_normal),
              variable  = c("alpha", paste0("beta_", colnames(X_normal)), "phi"),
              component = "magnitude_typical")
  )
  rownames(coef_table) <- NULL

  # ── Predictions on test set: mean-blend, matching every other model in
  # this project's fitting/evaluation convention ──────────────────────────
  post_logit   <- rstan::extract(fit_logit)
  post_extreme <- rstan::extract(fit_extreme)
  post_normal  <- rstan::extract(fit_normal)

  n_draws <- min(length(post_logit$alpha), length(post_extreme$alpha), length(post_normal$alpha))

  pred_draws      <- matrix(NA_real_, nrow = nrow(test), ncol = n_draws)
  p_extreme_draws <- matrix(NA_real_, nrow = nrow(test), ncol = n_draws)

  for (d in seq_len(n_draws)) {
    p_ext_d <- plogis(post_logit$alpha[d] + X_test_clf %*% post_logit$beta[d, ])

    mu_ext_d  <- exp(post_extreme$alpha[d] + X_test_ext %*% post_extreme$beta[d, ])
    mu_norm_d <- exp(post_normal$alpha[d]  + X_test_typ %*% post_normal$beta[d, ])

    pred_draws[, d]      <- p_ext_d * mu_ext_d + (1 - p_ext_d) * mu_norm_d
    p_extreme_draws[, d] <- p_ext_d
  }

  p_hat  <- apply(pred_draws, 1, median, na.rm = TRUE)
  p_sd   <- apply(pred_draws, 1, sd,    na.rm = TRUE)
  p_low  <- apply(pred_draws, 1, quantile, 0.025, na.rm = TRUE)
  p_high <- apply(pred_draws, 1, quantile, 0.975, na.rm = TRUE)
  p_extreme_mean <- apply(p_extreme_draws, 1, median, na.rm = TRUE)

  metrics <- compute_burned_metrics(y_test, p_hat, n_boot = n_boot, seed = seed)

  cat(sprintf("[mixture_formula] nRMSE    : %.4f (%.4f, %.4f)\n",
              metrics$nrmse, metrics$nrmse_ci[1], metrics$nrmse_ci[2]))
  cat(sprintf("[mixture_formula] Pearson r: %.4f (%.4f, %.4f)\n",
              metrics$cor, metrics$cor_ci[1], metrics$cor_ci[2]))
  cat(sprintf("[mixture_formula] Spearman : %.4f (%.4f, %.4f)\n",
              metrics$spearman, metrics$spearman_ci[1], metrics$spearman_ci[2]))

  pred_df <- tibble(
    lat = test$lat, lon = test$lon, year = test$year, month = test$month,
    burned_area_km2_total = y_test,
    burned_area_pred      = p_hat,
    residual              = y_test - p_hat,
    log_residual          = log(y_test + 1) - log(p_hat + 1),
    pred_sd    = p_sd,
    pred_low   = p_low,
    pred_high  = p_high,
    p_extreme  = p_extreme_mean
  )

  list(
    method            = "mixture_gamma_formula",
    formula_classifier = formula_classifier,   # stored as FORMULAS now,
    formula_extreme     = formula_extreme,      # not predictor-name vectors --
    formula_typical      = formula_typical,      # needed to rebuild identical
                                                  # design matrices at sampling time
    outcome           = outcome,
    threshold         = threshold,
    extreme_quantile  = extreme_quantile,
    fit_logit         = fit_logit,
    fit_extreme       = fit_extreme,
    fit_normal        = fit_normal,
    coef_table        = coef_table,
    predictions       = pred_df,
    metrics           = metrics,
    max_rhat          = max_rhat,
    max_rhat_logit    = rhat_logit,
    max_rhat_extreme  = rhat_extreme,
    max_rhat_normal   = rhat_normal,
    total_divergences = total_div,
    div_logit         = div_logit,
    div_extreme       = div_extreme,
    div_normal        = div_normal,
    compiled_model    = list(logistic = sm_logit, gamma = sm_gamma)
  )
}

View intercepts and coeffiencts:
```{r}
library(dplyr)
library(tidyr)
library(gt)

# =============================================================================
# Extracts posterior mean + 95% CI for every coefficient in every burned-area
# model fit ABOVE line 2177 of this Rmd: m1_bayes_ln, m1_bayes_g, m1_mixture,
# m2_bayes_ln, m2_bayes_g, m3-m9_mixture_custom.
#
# IMPORTANT CAVEAT: fit_burned_area_model() has THREE separate definitions in
# this file (lines 591, 1108, 3356). Rather than guess which one actually
# produced the model objects in your session, this script reads each model's
# ALREADY-STORED $coef_table directly -- whatever code actually ran, it
# already computed and saved this, so pulling it here is safe regardless of
# which duplicate definition was active. Worth deleting the two stale
# duplicates separately, but it doesn't affect this table's correctness.
# =============================================================================

fmt_param <- function(mean_val, lower_val, upper_val) {
  sprintf("%.3f [%.3f, %.3f]", mean_val, lower_val, upper_val)
}

# =============================================================================
# PART A: single-component models (m1_bayes_g, m1_bayes_ln, m2_bayes_g,
# m2_bayes_ln) -- coef_table has "variable" as raw Stan names (alpha,
# beta[1], beta[2], ..., sigma/phi), NOT yet mapped to real predictor names.
# Map positionally against the model's own predictor vector.
# =============================================================================
extract_single_component <- function(model_obj, model_label, predictors) {
  ct <- model_obj$coef_table

  mean_col  <- grep("^mean$", names(ct), value = TRUE)[1]
  lower_col <- grep("2\\.5", names(ct), value = TRUE)[1]
  upper_col <- grep("97\\.5", names(ct), value = TRUE)[1]

  if (is.na(mean_col) || is.na(lower_col) || is.na(upper_col)) {
    stop(sprintf("[%s] Could not find mean/2.5%%/97.5%% columns in coef_table. Actual columns: %s",
                 model_label, paste(names(ct), collapse = ", ")))
  }

  # alpha (intercept)
  alpha_row <- ct[ct$variable == "alpha", ]

  # beta[1], beta[2], ... -> map positionally to `predictors`, in order
  beta_rows <- ct[grepl("^beta\\[", ct$variable), ]
  beta_rows <- beta_rows[order(as.integer(gsub("beta\\[|\\]", "", beta_rows$variable))), ]

  if (nrow(beta_rows) != length(predictors)) {
    warning(sprintf(
      "[%s] Mismatch: %d beta rows in coef_table vs %d predictors supplied -- check the predictor vector matches what this model was actually fit with.",
      model_label, nrow(beta_rows), length(predictors)
    ))
  }

  out <- tibble(
    Model     = model_label,
    Component = "magnitude",
    Predictor = c("Intercept", predictors[seq_len(nrow(beta_rows))]),
    Estimate  = c(
      fmt_param(alpha_row[[mean_col]], alpha_row[[lower_col]], alpha_row[[upper_col]]),
      mapply(fmt_param, beta_rows[[mean_col]], beta_rows[[lower_col]], beta_rows[[upper_col]])
    )
  )

  # sigma (lognormal) or phi (gamma) -- dispersion, no predictor
  disp_row <- ct[ct$variable %in% c("sigma", "phi"), ]
  if (nrow(disp_row) == 1) {
    out <- bind_rows(out, tibble(
      Model = model_label, Component = "magnitude",
      Predictor = ifelse(disp_row$variable == "sigma", "Dispersion (\u03c3)", "Dispersion (\u03c6)"),
      Estimate = fmt_param(disp_row[[mean_col]], disp_row[[lower_col]], disp_row[[upper_col]])
    ))
  }

  out
}

# =============================================================================
# PART B: three-component mixture models (m1_mixture, m3-m9_mixture_custom)
# -- coef_table already has "variable" (alpha, beta_<predictor>, phi) AND
# "component" (classification / magnitude_extreme / magnitude_typical)
# correctly labeled. Just reshape into the same output format.
# =============================================================================
extract_mixture_model <- function(model_obj, model_label) {
  ct <- model_obj$coef_table

  # Column names like "2.5%"/"97.5%" get mangled by as.data.frame()'s
  # default check.names=TRUE (matrix -> data.frame conversion inside
  # fit_mixture_gamma_custom() itself, e.g. into "X2.5."/"X97.5."). Detect
  # the mean/lower/upper columns by pattern instead of a hardcoded exact
  # name, so this works regardless of the exact mangled form.
  mean_col  <- grep("^mean$", names(ct), value = TRUE)[1]
  lower_col <- grep("2\\.5", names(ct), value = TRUE)[1]
  upper_col <- grep("97\\.5", names(ct), value = TRUE)[1]

  if (is.na(mean_col) || is.na(lower_col) || is.na(upper_col)) {
    stop(sprintf("[%s] Could not find mean/2.5%%/97.5%% columns in coef_table. Actual columns: %s",
                 model_label, paste(names(ct), collapse = ", ")))
  }

  ct %>%
    mutate(
      Model = model_label,
      Component = recode(component,
                           "classification"     = "P(extreme)",
                           "magnitude_extreme"   = "Extreme fire: log(mean)",
                           "magnitude_typical"   = "Typical fire: log(mean)"),
      Predictor = case_when(
        variable == "alpha"        ~ "Intercept",
        variable == "phi"          ~ "Dispersion (\u03c6)",
        grepl("^beta_", variable)  ~ sub("^beta_", "", variable),
        TRUE                        ~ variable
      ),
      Estimate = fmt_param(.data[[mean_col]], .data[[lower_col]], .data[[upper_col]])
    ) %>%
    dplyr::select(Model, Component, Predictor, Estimate)
}

# =============================================================================
# BUILD: apply the two extractors to every model fit above line 2177
# =============================================================================
param_table_long <- bind_rows(
  extract_single_component(m1_bayes_ln, "m1: Log-normal (Bayes)", preds_m1),
  extract_single_component(m1_bayes_g,  "m1: Gamma (Bayes)",      preds_m1),
  extract_mixture_model(m1_mixture,     "m1: Mixture (original)"),

  extract_single_component(m2_bayes_ln, "m2: Log-normal (Bayes)", preds_m2),
  extract_single_component(m2_bayes_g,  "m2: Gamma (Bayes)",      preds_m2),

  extract_mixture_model(m3_mixture_custom, "m3: Mixture (custom)"),
  extract_mixture_model(m4_mixture_custom, "m4: Mixture (custom)"),
  extract_mixture_model(m5_mixture_custom, "m5: Mixture (custom)"),
  extract_mixture_model(m6_mixture_custom, "m6: Mixture (custom)"),
  extract_mixture_model(m7_mixture_custom, "m7: Mixture (custom)"),
  extract_mixture_model(m8_mixture_custom, "m8: Mixture (custom)"),
  extract_mixture_model(m9_mixture_custom, "m9: Mixture (custom)"),
  extract_mixture_model(m10_mixture_custom_truncated, "m10: Mixture (custom truncated)"),
  extract_mixture_model(m11_mixture_custom_truncated, "m11: Mixture (custom truncated)"),
  extract_mixture_model(m12_mixture_custom_truncated, "m12: Mixture (custom truncated)"),
  extract_mixture_model(m13_mixture_custom_truncated, "m13: Mixture (custom truncated)"),
  extract_mixture_model(m14_mixture_custom_truncated, "m14: Mixture (custom truncated)"),
  extract_mixture_model(m15_mixture_custom_truncated, "m15: Mixture (custom truncated)"),
  extract_mixture_model(m16_mixture_custom_truncated, "m16: Mixture (custom truncated)"),
  extract_mixture_model(m17_mixture_custom_truncated, "m17: Mixture (custom truncated)"),
  extract_mixture_model(m18_mixture_custom_truncated, "m18: Mixture (custom truncated)"),
  extract_mixture_model(m19_mixture_custom_truncated, "m19: Mixture (custom truncated)"),
  extract_mixture_model(m20_mixture_interactions, "m20: Mixture (custom truncated, interactions)")
)

# =============================================================================
# EXPORT: gt table -> LaTeX body only, grouped by Model then Component,
# matching the format used for the full-pipeline parameter table
# =============================================================================
export_table_body_only <- function(gt_tbl, path) {
  full_tex <- as_latex(gt_tbl) %>% as.character()
  body <- sub(".*(\\\\begin\\{tabular\\*\\}.*\\\\end\\{tabular\\*\\})[\\s\\S]*", "\\1", full_tex, perl = TRUE)
  writeLines(body, path)
}

print(param_table_long, n = Inf)

On m1's larger range (captures extremems): extra range is coming from: the whole distribution is inflated, not just the tail. m1_bayes_g's median (21.6) and mean (55.3) are both higher than m3's (22.2 median, 45.0 mean) despite m3's max being lower, and m1_bayes_g's 1st quartile (11.3) sits below m3's (14.1). This is the signature of a model that's systematically shifting more probability mass toward larger values across the board, not one that's specifically better at identifying which fires are the rare extreme ones while staying accurate on typical ones. That's exactly the failure mode the negative R² is diagnosing: a plain Gamma model applied uniformly, without a classifier separating extreme from typical fires, doesn't know when to predict big, it just predicts systematically bigger everywhere, which happens to stretch the tail further as a side effect but does so by overpredicting size broadly, not by correctly discriminating fire types.

cor(predictions_m3_mixture_custom$burned_area_pred,
    predictions_m3_mixture_custom$burned_area_km2_total, method = "spearman")

Covariate-dependent extreme-value models failed to converge regardless of predictor set size, consistent with the small number of extreme-fire observations (n≈70-96) relative to the demands of non-stationary extreme value estimation.

Also tried tighter priors so the sampler doesnt get stuck near 0. sigma's lower bound moved from 0 to 1 (structurally forbidding the collapse-to-zero solution), and xi is now hard-bounded to [-1, 1] (structurally forbidding it from drifting to -5.8). The prior on sigma is also now centered near your data's actual scale (mean excess ≈ 509) rather than near zero, giving the sampler a sensible starting region instead of leaving it to wander. Chains still did not converge

given the four separate model structures and now a deliberately constrained reparameterization all converging on the same degenerate result, this specific 55-observation extreme-fire sample doesn't support a stable GPD fit at all. Abandon GPD for this dataset. This is a tested limitation: extreme fire magnitudes in this record don't follow a form estimable with standard peaks-over-threshold methods at this sample size.

NRMSE and MAE: raw-scale error magnitude. Sensitive to the largest fires in the test set, since a few huge misses dominate both.

Pearson r / Spearman ρ: linear vs. rank agreement between predicted and observed size, on the raw scale.

R²: how much better the model does than just predicting the mean every time. Negative R² means the model is doing worse than a flat mean prediction — a real red flag, not just "low performance."

log_cor: correlation computed on log-transformed values, which matters specifically for right-skewed data like fire size, since it downweights the influence of the single largest fires and instead rewards getting the relative ordering right across the whole size range, including the many smaller fires that raw-scale metrics can end up ignoring. A higher value is  better. 

The biggest signal: R² sign. Every custom mixture model (m3–m8) has positive R² (0.076–0.090); the plain gamma models and the original mixture model (m1_bayes_g, m1_mixture, m2_bayes_g) are all negative (−0.61, −0.03, −0.42). That's not a close call, it means the three-part custom mixture structure (classifier + separate extreme/typical Gamma components) is the only family here that beats a trivial mean-prediction baseline at all. I'd rule out m1/m2 entirely on this basis alone, regardless of their competitive MAE.

Within the custom mixture family (m3–m8), two real contenders, not one clear winner:

m3 (U, tair): best NRMSE (3.49), best R² (0.090), best MAE (56.8) among all eight models. The simplest extreme-predictor set, and it wins on every raw-scale metric.

m4/m5 (U + C alongside precip terms): clearly best log_cor (0.470/0.469, vs. 0.428 for m3), at the cost of somewhat worse NRMSE/MAE than m3.But, a difference in log_cor between m4 and m3 of 0.042 is not statistically signitficane (p = 0.609, see next code chunk). Choosing to include C would be better justified by the Coffield et al. 2019 paper, and the fact that C doesn't hurt on any other metric. 

What this tells you about conifer cover specifically: the cleanest test is m6 vs. m7. identical predictor sets except C replaces U. m6 (with C, no U) is worse than m7 (with U, no C) on every single metric. So substituting conifer cover for burned-area-fraction doesn't help. But C added alongside U (m4/m5) produces the best log-scale correlation of the whole set — suggesting conifer cover helps the model rank fire sizes correctly across the full skewed distribution, even though it doesn't reduce raw-scale error.

Compare distributions after sampling. The above metrics measure how well the model's expected value tracks the pattern in real fire sizes across different climate/vegetation/urban conditions. If bigger fires tend to happen in drier, more remote conditions, a well-fit model's mean prediction should be correspondingly larger for those rows than for wetter, more urban-adjacent rows, and that pattern is exactly what correlation/R² detect. Whether any individual fire happens to land above or below its own row's specific mean (because of the Gamma's inherent randomness) is a separate question these metrics were never trying to answer, and shouldn't be expected to answer.

Coverage checks: for each test-set fire, does the model's fitted 95% interval (computable directly from its shape/rate without needing to sample — e.g., qgamma(c(0.025, 0.975), shape, rate)) actually contain the observed value roughly 95% of the time across the whole test set? Too-narrow intervals under-cover; too-wide intervals over-cover.

PIT (probability integral transform) histograms: compute pgamma(y_observed, shape, rate) for every test-set fire — if the model is well-calibrated, these values should be roughly uniformly distributed between 0 and 1; systematic skew reveals exactly where/how the fitted distribution's spread is wrong.

A sampled-draws comparison (generating actual rgamma() samples the way the full fire pipeline does, then comparing that distribution's summary statistics — spread, tail behavior — against the real observed distribution) is the more direct visual/distributional check, complementary to the mean-based accuracy metrics rather than a replacement for them. ie s-score. 

```{r}
library(dplyr)
library(data.table)
library(ggplot2)

# =============================================================================
# 1. SAMPLING: draws n_draws random samples from a fitted mixture model
#    (custom or custom_truncated). For the NON-truncated model, the extreme
#    component is drawn from an ordinary rgamma(). For the TRUNCATED model,
#    the extreme component is drawn from a Gamma truncated below at the
#    classification threshold, via REJECTION sampling (draw ordinary
#    rgamma() values, keep only those above threshold, repeat) -- this is
#    numerically stable regardless of how far into the tail the threshold
#    sits, unlike inverse-CDF sampling (qgamma() near probability 1 is
#    unstable and can produce astronomically large values).
# =============================================================================
sample_mixture_predictions <- function(model, test, n_draws = 500, seed = 123,
                                        truncate_extreme = NULL) {
  if (is.null(truncate_extreme)) {
    truncate_extreme <- grepl("truncated", model$method)
  }

  # Prefer stored FORMULAS (fit_mixture_gamma_formula()) when present --
  # these correctly preserve interaction terms. Fall back to the older
  # predictor-vector reconstruction (fit_mixture_gamma_custom[_truncated]())
  # for models that don't have formulas stored.
  if (!is.null(model$formula_classifier)) {
    fm_classifier <- update(model$formula_classifier, ~ . - 1)
    fm_extreme    <- update(model$formula_extreme,    ~ . - 1)
    fm_typical    <- update(model$formula_typical,    ~ . - 1)
  } else {
    preds_classifier <- if (!is.null(model$preds_classifier)) model$preds_classifier else model$predictors
    preds_extreme    <- if (!is.null(model$preds_extreme))    model$preds_extreme    else model$predictors
    preds_typical     <- if (!is.null(model$preds_typical))    model$preds_typical    else model$predictors

    if (is.null(preds_classifier) || is.null(preds_extreme) || is.null(preds_typical)) {
      stop(sprintf(
        "[%s] Could not find predictor names under formulas, split fields, or shared field. Actual fields: %s",
        model$method, paste(names(model), collapse = ", ")
      ))
    }

    fm_classifier <- as.formula(paste("~", paste(preds_classifier, collapse = " + "), "- 1"))
    fm_extreme    <- as.formula(paste("~", paste(preds_extreme,    collapse = " + "), "- 1"))
    fm_typical    <- as.formula(paste("~", paste(preds_typical,    collapse = " + "), "- 1"))
  }

  threshold <- model$threshold
  outcome   <- model$outcome

  X_test_clf <- model.matrix(fm_classifier, data = test)
  X_test_ext <- model.matrix(fm_extreme,    data = test)
  X_test_typ <- model.matrix(fm_typical,    data = test)

  post_logit   <- rstan::extract(model$fit_logit)
  post_extreme <- rstan::extract(model$fit_extreme)
  post_normal  <- rstan::extract(model$fit_normal)

  n_post <- min(length(post_logit$alpha), length(post_extreme$alpha), length(post_normal$alpha))
  set.seed(seed)
  draw_idx <- sample(seq_len(n_post), size = n_draws, replace = n_draws > n_post)

  n_test  <- nrow(test)
  sampled <- matrix(NA_real_, nrow = n_test, ncol = n_draws)
  is_ext_mat <- matrix(NA_integer_, nrow = n_test, ncol = n_draws)

  # Rejection-sampling truncated Gamma
  rgamma_truncated <- function(n, shape, rate, lower, max_attempts = 10000) {
    out <- numeric(n)
    needed <- rep(TRUE, n)
    attempts <- 0

    while (any(needed) && attempts < max_attempts) {
      candidates <- rgamma(sum(needed), shape = shape, rate = rate)
      accepted <- candidates > lower
      out[which(needed)[accepted]] <- candidates[accepted]
      needed[which(needed)[accepted]] <- FALSE
      attempts <- attempts + 1
    }

    if (any(needed)) {
      warning(sprintf(
        "%d of %d truncated-Gamma draws did not accept within %d attempts (shape/rate imply almost no mass above threshold=%.2f). Falling back to `lower` for these.",
        sum(needed), n, max_attempts, lower
      ))
      out[needed] <- lower
    }

    out
  }

  n_nonfinite_warned <- FALSE

  for (d in seq_len(n_draws)) {
    di <- draw_idx[d]

    p_ext_d <- as.numeric(plogis(post_logit$alpha[di] + X_test_clf %*% post_logit$beta[di, ]))
    is_ext  <- rbinom(n_test, size = 1, prob = p_ext_d)

    mu_ext_d   <- as.numeric(exp(post_extreme$alpha[di] + X_test_ext %*% post_extreme$beta[di, ]))
    phi_ext_d  <- post_extreme$phi[di]
    rate_ext_d <- phi_ext_d / mu_ext_d

    mu_typ_d   <- as.numeric(exp(post_normal$alpha[di] + X_test_typ %*% post_normal$beta[di, ]))
    phi_typ_d  <- post_normal$phi[di]
    rate_typ_d <- phi_typ_d / mu_typ_d

    # Guard: catch a genuinely broken upstream mu/rate immediately and
    # loudly, rather than let a non-finite value propagate silently into
    # rgamma()/rgamma_truncated() and produce an exploded result
    if (!n_nonfinite_warned && (any(!is.finite(mu_ext_d)) || any(!is.finite(rate_ext_d)) ||
                                 any(!is.finite(mu_typ_d)) || any(!is.finite(rate_typ_d)))) {
      warning(sprintf(
        "[%s] Non-finite mu/rate encountered at draw %d (posterior index %d). Check X_test_ext/X_test_typ column alignment against this model's fitted beta.",
        model$method, d, di
      ))
      n_nonfinite_warned <- TRUE
    }

    ext_draw <- if (truncate_extreme) {
      rgamma_truncated(n_test, shape = phi_ext_d, rate = rate_ext_d, lower = threshold)
    } else {
      rgamma(n_test, shape = phi_ext_d, rate = rate_ext_d)
    }
    typ_draw <- rgamma(n_test, shape = phi_typ_d, rate = rate_typ_d)

    sampled[, d]    <- ifelse(is_ext == 1, ext_draw, typ_draw)
    is_ext_mat[, d] <- is_ext
  }

  list(
    sampled_draws   = sampled,
    is_extreme_draw = is_ext_mat,
    observed        = test[[outcome]],
    n_draws         = n_draws,
    truncated       = truncate_extreme,
    model_label     = model$method
  )
}

# =============================================================================
# 2. METRICS: coverage, PIT, accuracy from the sampled mean
# =============================================================================
compute_sampled_metrics <- function(sample_result, n_boot = 1000, seed = 123) {
  sampled  <- sample_result$sampled_draws
  observed <- sample_result$observed
  n_test   <- nrow(sampled)

  lower <- apply(sampled, 1, quantile, probs = 0.025, na.rm = TRUE)
  upper <- apply(sampled, 1, quantile, probs = 0.975, na.rm = TRUE)
  covered <- (observed >= lower) & (observed <= upper)
  coverage_95 <- mean(covered, na.rm = TRUE)

  pit_values <- sapply(seq_len(n_test), function(i) {
    mean(sampled[i, ] <= observed[i], na.rm = TRUE)
  })

  pred_mean <- rowMeans(sampled, na.rm = TRUE)

  if (exists("compute_burned_metrics")) {
    accuracy <- compute_burned_metrics(observed, pred_mean, n_boot = n_boot, seed = seed)
  } else {
    accuracy <- list(
      nrmse = sqrt(mean((pred_mean - observed)^2, na.rm = TRUE)) / mean(observed, na.rm = TRUE),
      cor   = cor(pred_mean, observed, use = "complete.obs"),
      r2    = 1 - sum((observed - pred_mean)^2, na.rm = TRUE) /
                   sum((observed - mean(observed, na.rm = TRUE))^2, na.rm = TRUE)
    )
  }

  cat(sprintf("[%s] 95%% interval coverage: %.1f%% (target: 95%%)\n",
              sample_result$model_label, 100 * coverage_95))
  cat(sprintf("[%s] Mean PIT value: %.3f (target: 0.500 if well-calibrated)\n",
              sample_result$model_label, mean(pit_values, na.rm = TRUE)))

  list(
    coverage_95 = coverage_95,
    pit_values  = pit_values,
    lower_95    = lower,
    upper_95    = upper,
    accuracy_from_sampled_mean = accuracy
  )
}

# =============================================================================
# 3. HISTOGRAM: observed vs. sampled predicted distribution
# =============================================================================
plot_sampled_distribution <- function(sample_result, var_label, title = NULL,
                                       sscore_bins = 15, log_x = FALSE,
                                       remove_zeros = TRUE,
                                       low_width = 10, low_max = 100, high_width = 100) {

  n_draws <- sample_result$n_draws
  pred_vals_raw <- as.vector(sample_result$sampled_draws)
  obs_vals_raw  <- sample_result$observed

  pct_pred_zero <- mean(pred_vals_raw == 0, na.rm = TRUE) * 100
  pct_obs_zero  <- mean(obs_vals_raw == 0, na.rm = TRUE) * 100

  if (remove_zeros) {
    pred_vals <- pred_vals_raw[pred_vals_raw != 0]
    obs_vals  <- obs_vals_raw[obs_vals_raw != 0]
  } else {
    pred_vals <- pred_vals_raw
    obs_vals  <- obs_vals_raw
  }

  max_val <- max(c(pred_vals, obs_vals), na.rm = TRUE)

  # Custom piecewise bin scheme: fine (low_width) bins from 0 to low_max,
  # coarser (high_width) bins above that, up through the actual max value
  low_breaks <- seq(0, low_max, by = low_width)
  if (max_val > low_max) {
    high_breaks <- seq(low_max + high_width, ceiling(max_val / high_width) * high_width, by = high_width)
    breaks <- c(low_breaks, high_breaks)
  } else {
    breaks <- low_breaks
  }

  pred_binned <- data.table(bin = cut(pred_vals, breaks = breaks, include.lowest = TRUE))
  obs_binned  <- data.table(bin = cut(obs_vals,  breaks = breaks, include.lowest = TRUE))

  bin_levels <- levels(pred_binned$bin)

  pred_counts <- pred_binned[, .(count = .N / n_draws), by = bin]
  obs_counts  <- obs_binned[, .(count = .N), by = bin]

  pred_counts[, source := "Predicted (sampled)"]
  obs_counts[, source  := "Observed"]

  combined <- rbind(pred_counts, obs_counts)
  combined[, bin := factor(bin, levels = bin_levels)]

  bin_lookup <- data.table(
    bin = factor(bin_levels, levels = bin_levels),
    bin_lower = breaks[-length(breaks)],
    bin_upper = breaks[-1]
  )
  combined <- merge(combined, bin_lookup, by = "bin")

  # Shrink the TOTAL bin width slightly (inset_frac) so there's a visible
  # gap BETWEEN adjacent bins, not just between the two source-halves
  # within one bin -- this is what fixes the "fused into one weird-width
  # bar" look from before.
  inset_frac <- 0.10   # 10% of bin width reserved as inter-bin gap
  gap_frac   <- 0.05   # 5% of the remaining width as the intra-bin gap

  combined[, `:=`(
    bin_span   = bin_upper - bin_lower,
    bin_inset  = (bin_upper - bin_lower) * inset_frac / 2
  )]
  combined[, `:=`(
    inset_lower = bin_lower + bin_inset,
    inset_upper = bin_upper - bin_inset
  )]
  combined[, bin_mid_split := (inset_lower + inset_upper) / 2]

  combined[source == "Observed", `:=`(
    xmin = inset_lower,
    xmax = bin_mid_split - (inset_upper - inset_lower) * gap_frac / 2
  )]
  combined[source == "Predicted (sampled)", `:=`(
    xmin = bin_mid_split + (inset_upper - inset_lower) * gap_frac / 2,
    xmax = inset_upper
  )]

  summary_stats <- rbind(
    data.table(source = "Predicted (sampled)", stat = "Max", value = max(pred_vals, na.rm = TRUE)),
    data.table(source = "Observed",            stat = "Max", value = max(obs_vals,  na.rm = TRUE))
  )

  metric_label <- ""
  if (exists("compute_sscore")) {
    pred_dt <- data.table(
      draw_id = rep(seq_len(n_draws), each = nrow(sample_result$sampled_draws)),
      value   = as.vector(sample_result$sampled_draws)
    )
    if (remove_zeros) {
      pred_dt   <- pred_dt[value != 0]
      obs_nonzero <- obs_vals_raw[obs_vals_raw != 0]
    } else {
      obs_nonzero <- obs_vals_raw
    }
    sscore_draws <- compute_sscore(pred_dt, obs_nonzero, sscore_bins, bin_method = "quantile_union")
    sscore_mean  <- mean(sscore_draws)
    sscore_ci    <- quantile(sscore_draws, c(0.025, 0.975))
    metric_label <- sprintf("S-score: %.2f [%.2f, %.2f]", sscore_mean, sscore_ci[1], sscore_ci[2])
  }

  zero_label <- sprintf("Zeros removed:\nPredicted: %.1f%%\nObserved: %.1f%%\n%s\n%s",
                         if (remove_zeros) pct_pred_zero else 0,
                         if (remove_zeros) pct_obs_zero  else 0,
                         metric_label,
                         ifelse(sample_result$truncated, "(truncated extreme sampling)", "(untruncated)"))

  p <- ggplot() +
    geom_rect(data = combined, aes(xmin = xmin, xmax = xmax, ymin = 0, ymax = count, fill = source)) +
    geom_vline(data = summary_stats,
               aes(xintercept = value, color = source, linetype = stat),
               linewidth = 0.7) +
    scale_fill_manual(values = c("Observed" = "firebrick", "Predicted (sampled)" = "steelblue"), name = NULL) +
    scale_color_manual(values = c("Observed" = "firebrick", "Predicted (sampled)" = "steelblue"), guide = "none") +
    scale_linetype_manual(values = c("Max" = "dotted"), name = NULL) +
    guides(linetype = guide_legend(override.aes = list(color = "black"))) +
    annotate("text", x = Inf, y = Inf, label = zero_label,
             hjust = 1.05, vjust = 1.1, size = 3.0, color = "black") +
    labs(title = title, x = var_label, y = "Count", fill = NULL) +
    theme_minimal()

  if (log_x) p <- p + scale_x_log10()
  p
}
```

# =============================================================================
# Sampling + metrics + histogram for every MIXTURE-family model (m1_mixture
# and m3-m19, the three-component classifier+extreme+typical models).
# The single-component models (m1_bayes_g, m1_bayes_ln, m2_bayes_g,
# m2_bayes_ln) are NOT mixture models -- they have no $fit_logit/$fit_extreme/
# $fit_normal, so sample_mixture_predictions() doesn't apply to them and
# they're deliberately excluded here.
# =============================================================================

mixture_model_names <- c(
  "m1_mixture",
  paste0("m", 3:19, "_mixture_custom", ifelse(3:19 >= 10, "_truncated", "")), "m20_mixture_interactions"
)

# Sanity check: confirm every name actually exists as an object before
# looping, so a typo/missing model fails loudly and immediately rather
# than partway through an 18-model loop
missing_models <- mixture_model_names[!sapply(mixture_model_names, exists)]
if (length(missing_models) > 0) {
  stop("These model objects were not found in the environment: ",
       paste(missing_models, collapse = ", "))
}

cat(sprintf("Running sampling + metrics + plots for %d mixture models...\n", length(mixture_model_names)))
cat("This does 500 draws x matrix multiplication per model -- may take a while.\n\n")

samples_list <- list()
metrics_list <- list()
plots_list   <- list()

for (nm in mixture_model_names) {
  cat(sprintf("=== %s ===\n", nm))
  model_obj <- get(nm)

  samples_list[[nm]] <- sample_mixture_predictions(model_obj, test, n_draws = 500)
  metrics_list[[nm]] <- compute_sampled_metrics(samples_list[[nm]])
  plots_list[[nm]]   <- plot_sampled_distribution(
    samples_list[[nm]], "Burned area (km\u00b2)",
    title = nm, log_x = FALSE,
    low_width = 25, low_max = 100, high_width = 25
  )

  cat("\n")
}

# =============================================================================
# Quick-access summary table: coverage + PIT mean + accuracy, one row per
# model, so you can scan all 18 at once before opening any individual plot
# =============================================================================
sampled_summary <- do.call(rbind, lapply(names(metrics_list), function(nm) {
  m <- metrics_list[[nm]]
  data.frame(
    model        = nm,
    coverage_95  = m$coverage_95,
    mean_pit     = mean(m$pit_values, na.rm = TRUE),
    nrmse        = m$accuracy_from_sampled_mean$nrmse,
    cor          = m$accuracy_from_sampled_mean$cor,
    r2           = if (!is.null(m$accuracy_from_sampled_mean$r2)) m$accuracy_from_sampled_mean$r2 else NA
  )
}))

print(sampled_summary)

plot_observed_vs_predicted_gridcell_year <- function(sample_result, var_label, title = NULL,
                                                       remove_zeros = TRUE, log_scale = TRUE) {

  n_draws <- sample_result$n_draws

  dt <- data.table(
    lat  = sample_result$lat,
    lon  = sample_result$lon,
    year = sample_result$year,
    observed = sample_result$observed
  )
  pred_dt <- as.data.table(sample_result$sampled_draws)
  setnames(pred_dt, paste0("draw_", seq_len(n_draws)))
  dt <- cbind(dt, pred_dt)

  # Observed: total burned area per gridcell-year (fixed, single value)
  obs_agg <- dt[, .(observed_total = sum(observed)), by = .(lat, lon, year)]

  # Predicted: total burned area per gridcell-year, PER DRAW, then
  # summarize mean + 95% CI across draws
  draw_cols <- paste0("draw_", seq_len(n_draws))
  pred_agg <- dt[, lapply(.SD, sum), by = .(lat, lon, year), .SDcols = draw_cols]
  pred_agg[, pred_mean  := apply(.SD, 1, mean),     .SDcols = draw_cols]
  pred_agg[, pred_lower := apply(.SD, 1, quantile, probs = 0.025), .SDcols = draw_cols]
  pred_agg[, pred_upper := apply(.SD, 1, quantile, probs = 0.975), .SDcols = draw_cols]

  plot_data <- merge(obs_agg, pred_agg[, .(lat, lon, year, pred_mean, pred_lower, pred_upper)],
                      by = c("lat", "lon", "year"))
  setnames(plot_data, "observed_total", "observed")

  plot_data[, covered := observed >= pred_lower & observed <= pred_upper]

  if (remove_zeros) {
    plot_data <- plot_data[observed != 0]
  }

  coverage_pct <- mean(plot_data$covered, na.rm = TRUE) * 100

  p <- ggplot(plot_data, aes(x = observed, y = pred_mean)) +
    geom_abline(slope = 1, intercept = 0, linetype = "dashed", color = "grey40") +
    geom_errorbar(aes(ymin = pred_lower, ymax = pred_upper, color = covered),
                  width = 0, alpha = 0.5, linewidth = 0.4) +
    geom_point(aes(color = covered), size = 1.3, alpha = 0.7) +
    scale_color_manual(
      values = c("TRUE" = "steelblue", "FALSE" = "firebrick"),
      labels = c("TRUE" = "95% CI covers observed", "FALSE" = "95% CI misses observed"),
      name = NULL
    ) +
    annotate("text", x = -Inf, y = Inf,
             label = sprintf("Coverage: %.1f%%\nn = %d gridcell-years\n%s",
                              coverage_pct, nrow(plot_data),
                              ifelse(sample_result$truncated, "(truncated extreme sampling)", "(untruncated)")),
             hjust = -0.05, vjust = 1.2, size = 3.0, color = "black") +
    labs(title = title, x = paste("Observed", var_label), y = paste("Predicted mean", var_label)) +
    theme_minimal()

  if (log_scale) {
    p <- p + scale_x_log10() + scale_y_log10()
  }

  p
}

for (nm in c("m3_mixture_custom", "m4_mixture_custom", "m5_mixture_custom",

}

2007 and 20010 saw frequent, small fires compared with other years. 
2004 and 2005 saw more severe fires. 
Does m20, which includes interactions, capture these years of small vs. large fires, indipendant of fire count?

```{r}
plot_severity_obs_vs_pred <- function(severity_dt, plot_years = NULL,
                                       highlight_years = c(2004, 2005, 2007, 2010),
                                       title = NULL, log_scale = TRUE) {

  # plot_years: NULL (default) plots every gridcell-year, colored by
  # whether it's one of highlight_years or "Other years". If plot_years
  # is supplied (e.g. c(2010), or c(2002, 2004, 2008)), the plot is
  # RESTRICTED to only those years -- points are then colored per
  # individual year, and highlight_years is ignored for the color
  # mapping (every plotted year gets its own color, since you've
  # already chosen exactly which years you want to see).
  if (!is.null(plot_years)) {
    dt <- severity_dt[year %in% plot_years]
    dt[, year_group := factor(as.character(year), levels = as.character(sort(unique(plot_years))))]

    n_years <- length(unique(dt$year_group))
    palette <- if (n_years <= 8) {
      c("#D55E00", "#009E73", "#0072B2", "#CC79A7", "#F0E442", "#56B4E9", "#E69F00", "#000000")[seq_len(n_years)]
    } else {
      scales::hue_pal()(n_years)  # fall back to an evenly-spaced hue palette if more than 8 years requested
    }
    color_values <- setNames(palette, levels(dt$year_group))
    legend_title <- "Year"
  } else {
    dt <- copy(severity_dt)
    dt[, year_group := ifelse(year %in% highlight_years, as.character(year), "Other years")]
    dt[, year_group := factor(year_group, levels = c(as.character(highlight_years), "Other years"))]
    color_values <- c(setNames(c("#D55E00", "#009E73", "#0072B2", "#CC79A7"), as.character(highlight_years)),
                       "Other years" = "grey70")
    legend_title <- "Year"
  }

  p <- ggplot(dt, aes(x = severity_observed, y = severity_pred_mean)) +
    geom_abline(slope = 1, intercept = 0, linetype = "dashed", color = "grey40") +
    geom_errorbar(aes(ymin = severity_pred_lower, ymax = severity_pred_upper, color = year_group),
                  width = 0, alpha = 0.4, linewidth = 0.4) +
    geom_point(aes(color = year_group), size = 1.6, alpha = 0.8) +
    scale_color_manual(values = color_values, name = legend_title) +
    labs(title = title,
         x = "Observed severity (burned area / fire count, km\u00b2)",
         y = "Predicted severity (burned area / fire count, km\u00b2)") +
    theme_minimal()

  if (log_scale) p <- p + scale_x_log10() + scale_y_log10()
  p
}

# Restrict to just one year
plot_severity_obs_vs_pred(severity_m20, plot_years = c(2010), title = "m20: 2010 only", log_scale = FALSE)
plot_severity_obs_vs_pred(severity_m20, plot_years = c(2007), title = "m20: 2007 only", log_scale = FALSE)
plot_severity_obs_vs_pred(severity_m20, plot_years = c(2004), title = "m20: 2004 only", log_scale = FALSE)
plot_severity_obs_vs_pred(severity_m20, plot_years = c(2005), title = "m20: 2005 only", log_scale = FALSE)
# Restrict to a specific custom set
plot_severity_obs_vs_pred(severity_m20, plot_years = c(2004, 2005), title = "m20: 2004, 2005", log_scale = FALSE)

plot_severity_obs_vs_pred(severity_m20, plot_years = c(2007, 2010), title = "m20: 2007, 2010", log_scale = FALSE)

Does the classifier corrrectly identify small vs large fires - this may get to the bottom of the many small vs sever regime differences. 


```{r}
library(pROC)

# =============================================================================
# Per-fire classifier diagnostic: does m20's classifier correctly separate
# true extreme (>= threshold) from true typical (< threshold) fires,
# independent of the magnitude models entirely?
# =============================================================================
build_classifier_diagnostic <- function(sample_result, threshold, test) {
  p_ext_mean <- rowMeans(sample_result$is_extreme_draw, na.rm = TRUE)  # fraction of 500 draws classifying this fire extreme

  dt <- data.table(
    lat        = sample_result$lat,
    lon        = sample_result$lon,
    year       = sample_result$year,
    observed   = sample_result$observed,
    p_extreme  = p_ext_mean,
    true_extreme = sample_result$observed >= threshold
  )
  dt
}

clf_m20 <- build_classifier_diagnostic(samples_list[["m20_mixture_interactions"]], threshold = 254.2795, test = test)

# ---- 1. ROC / AUC: overall classifier discrimination ----
cat(sprintf("Classifier AUC: %.3f\n", pROC::auc(roc_obj)))
plot(roc_obj, main = sprintf("m20 classifier ROC (AUC = %.3f)", pROC::auc(roc_obj)))


# ---- 2. Distribution of P(extreme) split by TRUE label -- the cleanest
# single check of separation. Well-separated: true-typical fires cluster
# near 0, true-extreme fires cluster near 1. Poor separation (relevant to
# your hypothesis): true-typical fires with meaningfully elevated P(extreme). ----
ggplot(clf_m20, aes(x = true_extreme, y = p_extreme)) +
  geom_jitter(width = 0.15, alpha = 0.4, size = 1.3, color = "steelblue") +
  geom_boxplot(width = 0.3, alpha = 0.3, outlier.shape = NA) +
  scale_x_discrete(labels = c("FALSE" = "True: typical (< threshold)", "TRUE" = "True: extreme (\u2265 threshold)")) +
  labs(title = "m20: classifier-predicted P(extreme) by true fire class",
       x = NULL, y = "Mean P(extreme) across 500 draws") +
  theme_minimal()

# ---- 3. THE KEY CHECK FOR YOUR HYPOTHESIS: among TRUE typical (small)
# fires only, is P(extreme) elevated specifically in 2007/2010 relative
# to other years? This directly tests whether the model can represent a
# "many genuinely small fires" year without spuriously extreme-classifying
# some of them. ----
clf_m20[, year_group := fifelse(year %in% c(2007, 2010), "2007/2010 (many small)",
                          fifelse(year %in% c(2004, 2005), "2004/2005 (severe)", "Other years"))]

true_typical_only <- clf_m20[true_extreme == FALSE]

ggplot(true_typical_only, aes(x = year_group, y = p_extreme)) +
  geom_jitter(width = 0.15, alpha = 0.4, size = 1.3, aes(color = year_group)) +
  geom_boxplot(width = 0.3, alpha = 0.3, outlier.shape = NA) +
  scale_color_manual(values = c("2007/2010 (many small)" = "#0072B2",
                                  "2004/2005 (severe)"     = "#D55E00",
                                  "Other years"             = "grey60"), guide = "none") +
  labs(title = "m20: P(extreme) among TRULY TYPICAL (small) fires only, by year group",
       subtitle = "If 2007/2010 shows elevated P(extreme) here, the model is spuriously\ninflating some genuinely small fires toward the extreme component",
       x = NULL, y = "Mean P(extreme) across 500 draws") +
  theme_minimal()

cat("\nMean P(extreme) among true-typical fires, by year group:\n")
print(true_typical_only[, .(mean_p_extreme = mean(p_extreme), n = .N), by = year_group])
```

- Overall accuracygood, AUC=0.887 and the specific pattern, year-conditional bias looks good. The classifier does make individual mistakes, a few true-typical fires get elevated P(extreme), a few true-extreme fires get a lowish one, but this is ordinary classifier noise at this AUC level, not a systematic failure. The mean bynyear group table: 0.031, 0.039, 0.035. No meaningful difference across year groups. If the classifier's imperfections were what's driving the regime-difference problem, expect 2007/2010 specifically to show elevated misclassification relative to the other groups, and it doesn't. So: real, but non-year-specific classifier noise, not the mechanism behind the regime failure. 

Next, test the two Gamma components: predicted burned areas for fires classified as extreme, versus fires classified as typical. This might reveal whether the two gamma models are too similar to carry over the classification into predictions of butned area. .
```{r}
library(dplyr)
library(data.table)
library(ggplot2)

# =============================================================================
# For each posterior draw, split predicted burned area by which component
# (extreme vs. typical) actually generated it that draw -- using
# is_extreme_draw, the per-draw classification outcome already stored in
# sample_mixture_predictions()'s output. This directly compares the two
# Gamma components' OUTPUT distributions, to check whether classification
# is actually carrying through to meaningfully different predictions.
# =============================================================================
compare_component_outputs <- function(sample_result, threshold) {
  sampled  <- sample_result$sampled_draws       # n_test x n_draws
  is_ext   <- sample_result$is_extreme_draw       # n_test x n_draws, same shape

  # Flatten both matrices in parallel, tagging each (fire, draw) cell by
  # which component generated it
  dt <- data.table(
    predicted_value = as.vector(sampled),
    component       = as.vector(is_ext)
  )
  dt[, component := fifelse(component == 1, "Classified extreme", "Classified typical")]

  dt
}

build_classifier_diagnostic <- function(sample_result, threshold, test) {
  p_ext_mean <- rowMeans(sample_result$is_extreme_draw, na.rm = TRUE)

  dt <- data.table(
    lat        = sample_result$lat,
    lon        = sample_result$lon,
    year       = sample_result$year,
    observed   = sample_result$observed,
    p_extreme  = p_ext_mean,
    true_extreme = sample_result$observed >= threshold
  )
  dt

Sensitivity analysis: feed both gamma models with the full test set (exclude the classification model) to anser: "how different are the simulated distributions between the typical veruss extreme gamma models?"

```{r}
library(dplyr)
library(data.table)
library(ggplot2)

# =============================================================================
# SENSITIVITY TEST: feed the FULL test set through BOTH Gamma components
# independently (ignoring classification entirely), to compare how
# differently the extreme and typical sub-models behave in isolation.
# =============================================================================
sensitivity_test_gamma_components <- function(model, test, n_draws = 500, seed = 123,
                                                truncate_extreme = FALSE) {

  if (!is.null(model$formula_extreme)) {
    fm_extreme <- update(model$formula_extreme, ~ . - 1)
    fm_typical <- update(model$formula_typical, ~ . - 1)
  } else {
    preds_extreme <- if (!is.null(model$preds_extreme)) model$preds_extreme else model$predictors
    preds_typical <- if (!is.null(model$preds_typical)) model$preds_typical else model$predictors
    fm_extreme <- as.formula(paste("~", paste(preds_extreme, collapse = " + "), "- 1"))
    fm_typical <- as.formula(paste("~", paste(preds_typical, collapse = " + "), "- 1"))
  }

  threshold <- model$threshold

  X_test_ext <- model.matrix(fm_extreme, data = test)
  X_test_typ <- model.matrix(fm_typical, data = test)

  post_extreme <- rstan::extract(model$fit_extreme)
  post_normal  <- rstan::extract(model$fit_normal)

  n_post <- min(length(post_extreme$alpha), length(post_normal$alpha))
  set.seed(seed)
  draw_idx <- sample(seq_len(n_post), size = n_draws, replace = n_draws > n_post)

  n_test <- nrow(test)
  extreme_draws <- matrix(NA_real_, nrow = n_test, ncol = n_draws)
  typical_draws <- matrix(NA_real_, nrow = n_test, ncol = n_draws)

  rgamma_truncated <- function(n, shape, rate, lower, max_attempts = 10000) {
    out <- numeric(n)
    needed <- rep(TRUE, n)
    attempts <- 0
    while (any(needed) && attempts < max_attempts) {
      candidates <- rgamma(sum(needed), shape = shape, rate = rate)
      accepted <- candidates > lower
      out[which(needed)[accepted]] <- candidates[accepted]
      needed[which(needed)[accepted]] <- FALSE
      attempts <- attempts + 1
    }
    if (any(needed)) out[needed] <- lower
    out
  }

  for (d in seq_len(n_draws)) {
    di <- draw_idx[d]

    mu_ext_d   <- as.numeric(exp(post_extreme$alpha[di] + X_test_ext %*% post_extreme$beta[di, ]))
    phi_ext_d  <- post_extreme$phi[di]
    rate_ext_d <- phi_ext_d / mu_ext_d

    mu_typ_d   <- as.numeric(exp(post_normal$alpha[di] + X_test_typ %*% post_normal$beta[di, ]))
    phi_typ_d  <- post_normal$phi[di]
    rate_typ_d <- phi_typ_d / mu_typ_d

    # EVERY test row goes through BOTH components, regardless of classification
    extreme_draws[, d] <- if (truncate_extreme) {
      rgamma_truncated(n_test, shape = phi_ext_d, rate = rate_ext_d, lower = threshold)
    } else {
      rgamma(n_test, shape = phi_ext_d, rate = rate_ext_d)
    }
    typical_draws[, d] <- rgamma(n_test, shape = phi_typ_d, rate = rate_typ_d)
  }

  list(extreme_draws = extreme_draws, typical_draws = typical_draws,
       truncated = truncate_extreme, threshold = threshold)
}

# =============================================================================
# PLOT + SUMMARY: compare the two components' full-test-set distributions
# =============================================================================
plot_sensitivity_test <- function(sens_result, title = NULL) {
  dt <- data.table(
    predicted_value = c(as.vector(sens_result$extreme_draws), as.vector(sens_result$typical_draws)),
    model = rep(c("Extreme model (all fires)", "Typical model (all fires)"),
                times = c(length(sens_result$extreme_draws), length(sens_result$typical_draws)))
  )

  cat("Summary, full test set through EACH component independently:\n")
  print(dt[predicted_value > 0, .(
    median = median(predicted_value), mean = mean(predicted_value),
    p75 = quantile(predicted_value, 0.75), p95 = quantile(predicted_value, 0.95),
    max = max(predicted_value), n = .N
  ), by = model])

  # Approximate KS test on the pooled distributions -- note: draws from the
  # same posterior sample are reused across many test rows, so this is a
  # descriptive/approximate comparison of distributional SHAPE, not a
  # formally independent-sample hypothesis test
  ks_result <- suppressWarnings(ks.test(sens_result$extreme_draws[sens_result$extreme_draws > 0],
                                          sens_result$typical_draws[sens_result$typical_draws > 0]))
  cat(sprintf("\nApproximate KS statistic (distributional overlap): D = %.3f, p %s 0.001\n",
              ks_result$statistic, ifelse(ks_result$p.value < 0.001, "<", paste("=", round(ks_result$p.value, 4)))))

  p <- ggplot(dt[predicted_value > 0], aes(x = predicted_value, fill = model)) +
    geom_density(alpha = 0.5) +
    scale_fill_manual(values = c("Extreme model (all fires)" = "#D55E00", "Typical model (all fires)" = "#0072B2")) +
    geom_vline(xintercept = sens_result$threshold, linetype = "dashed", color = "grey30") +
    labs(title = title,
         subtitle = sprintf("Dashed line: extreme threshold (%.1f km\u00b2) %s",
                             sens_result$threshold,
                             ifelse(sens_result$truncated, "| extreme model TRUNCATED", "| extreme model UNTRUNCATED")),
         x = "Predicted burned area (km\u00b2, log scale)", y = "Density", fill = NULL) +
    theme_minimal()

  p
}

# =============================================================================
# RUN: m20, both truncated and untruncated, compared side by side
# =============================================================================
sens_m20_untrunc <- sensitivity_test_gamma_components(m20_mixture_interactions, test, n_draws = 500,
                                                        truncate_extreme = FALSE)
sens_m20_trunc   <- sensitivity_test_gamma_components(m20_mixture_interactions, test, n_draws = 500,
                                                        truncate_extreme = TRUE)

hist(sens_m20_trunc$extreme_draws, xlim=c(threshold, max(sens_m20_trunc$extreme_draws)))
hist(sens_m20_trunc$typical_draws)

hist(sens_m20_trunc$extreme_draws, xlim = c(threshold, max(sens_m20_trunc$extreme_draws)),
     freq = FALSE, main = "Extreme model (truncated), full test set",
     xlab = "Predicted burned area (km\u00b2)")

hist(sens_m20_trunc$typical_draws, freq = FALSE,
     main = "Typical model, full test set",
     xlab = "Predicted burned area (km\u00b2)")

p_untrunc <- plot_sensitivity_test(sens_m20_untrunc, title = "m20: full test set through both components (UNTRUNCATED)")
p_trunc   <- plot_sensitivity_test(sens_m20_trunc,   title = "m20: full test set through both components (TRUNCATED)")

p_untrunc + scale_x_log10() 
p_trunc + scale_x_log10() 

p_untrunc + xlim(5, max(sens_m20_untrunc$extreme_draws))
p_trunc + xlim(5, max(sens_m20_trunc$extreme_draws))
```

Reliability diagram for m20's extreme classifier:
Recomputes p_ext_d DIRECTLY from the posterior (not from the sampled binary is_extreme_draw outcomes), since a reliability diagram needs the continuous predicted probability, not a Monte Carlo-sampled 0/1 draw.
```{r}
compute_burned_area_reliability_by_draw <- function(model, test, n_bins = 10, n_draws = 500, seed = 123) {

  if (!is.null(model$formula_classifier)) {
    fm_classifier <- update(model$formula_classifier, ~ . - 1)
  } else {
    preds_classifier <- if (!is.null(model$preds_classifier)) model$preds_classifier else model$predictors
    fm_classifier <- as.formula(paste("~", paste(preds_classifier, collapse = " + "), "- 1"))
  }

  X_test_clf <- model.matrix(fm_classifier, data = test)
  threshold  <- model$threshold
  true_extreme <- as.integer(test[[model$outcome]] >= threshold)

  post_logit <- rstan::extract(model$fit_logit)
  n_post <- length(post_logit$alpha)
  set.seed(seed)
  draw_idx <- sample(seq_len(n_post), size = n_draws, replace = n_draws > n_post)

  # p_ext_d for every draw, pooled, to set FIXED bin edges shared across draws
  p_ext_all_draws <- sapply(draw_idx, function(di) {
    as.numeric(plogis(post_logit$alpha[di] + X_test_clf %*% post_logit$beta[di, ]))
  })

  bin_probs <- seq(0, 1, length.out = n_bins + 1)
  breaks <- unique(quantile(as.vector(p_ext_all_draws), probs = bin_probs, na.rm = TRUE))
  bin_levels <- levels(cut(as.vector(p_ext_all_draws), breaks = breaks, include.lowest = TRUE))

  rel_by_draw <- rbindlist(lapply(seq_len(n_draws), function(d) {
    p_ext_d <- p_ext_all_draws[, d]
    bin <- cut(p_ext_d, breaks = breaks, include.lowest = TRUE)

    dt <- data.table(bin = factor(bin, levels = bin_levels), p_ext_d = p_ext_d, true_extreme = true_extreme)
    dt[, .(
      mean_predicted = mean(p_ext_d),
      observed_rate  = mean(true_extreme),
      n_fires        = .N
    ), by = bin][, draw_id := d]
  }))

  rel_by_draw
}

plot_burned_area_reliability <- function(model, test, n_bins = 10, n_draws = 500, seed = 123,
                                          title = NULL) {

  rel_by_draw <- compute_burned_area_reliability_by_draw(model, test, n_bins, n_draws, seed)

  rel_summary <- rel_by_draw[, .(
    mean_predicted_avg   = mean(mean_predicted),
    mean_predicted_lower = quantile(mean_predicted, 0.025),
    mean_predicted_upper = quantile(mean_predicted, 0.975),
    observed_rate_avg    = mean(observed_rate),
    observed_rate_lower  = quantile(observed_rate, 0.025),
    observed_rate_upper  = quantile(observed_rate, 0.975),
    n_fires_avg          = mean(n_fires)
  ), by = bin][order(mean_predicted_avg)]

  p <- ggplot(rel_summary, aes(x = mean_predicted_avg, y = observed_rate_avg)) +
    geom_abline(slope = 1, intercept = 0, linetype = "dashed", color = "grey40", linewidth = 0.5) +
    geom_errorbar(aes(ymin = observed_rate_lower, ymax = observed_rate_upper),
                  width = 0, alpha = 0.6, color = "firebrick", linewidth = 0.6) +
    geom_errorbarh(aes(xmin = mean_predicted_lower, xmax = mean_predicted_upper),
                   height = 0, alpha = 0.6, color = "black", linewidth = 0.5) +
    geom_line(color = "black", linewidth = 0.6) +
    geom_point(aes(size = n_fires_avg), color = "black", alpha = 0.75) +
    scale_size_continuous(name = "Mean fires\nin bin", range = c(2, 10)) +
    labs(title = title,
         x = "Mean predicted P(extreme) (bin)",
         y = "Observed extreme-fire rate (fires \u2265 threshold / fires in bin)") +
    theme_minimal(base_size = 13) +
    theme(
      panel.grid.minor = element_blank(),
      plot.title = element_text(face = "bold", size = 14),
      axis.title = element_text(size = 12),
      legend.title = element_text(size = 11),
      legend.text = element_text(size = 10)
    )

  p
}

  m20_mixture_interactions, test, n_bins = 10, n_draws = 500,
  title = "m20: extreme-fire classifier reliability"
)
p_reliability_m20

#-------------
# CLASSIFIER
#-------------
build_classifier_diagnostic <- function(sample_result, threshold, test) {
  p_ext_mean <- rowMeans(sample_result$is_extreme_draw, na.rm = TRUE)

  dt <- data.table(
    lat        = sample_result$lat,
    lon        = sample_result$lon,
    year       = sample_result$year,
    observed   = sample_result$observed,
    p_extreme  = p_ext_mean,
    true_extreme = sample_result$observed >= threshold
  )
  dt
}

clf_m <- build_classifier_diagnostic(samples_list[["m12_mixture_custom_truncated"]], threshold = 254.2795, test = test)

# ---- 1. ROC / AUC: rebuilt from clf_m, NOT reused from any earlier model ----
roc_obj <- pROC::roc(clf_m$true_extreme, clf_m$p_extreme, quiet = TRUE)
cat(sprintf("Classifier AUC: %.3f\n", pROC::auc(roc_obj)))
plot(roc_obj, main = sprintf("Classifier ROC (AUC = %.3f)", pROC::auc(roc_obj)))

# ---- 2. Distribution of P(extreme) split by TRUE label ----
ggplot(clf_m, aes(x = true_extreme, y = p_extreme)) +
  geom_jitter(width = 0.15, alpha = 0.4, size = 1.3, color = "steelblue") +
  geom_boxplot(width = 0.3, alpha = 0.3, outlier.shape = NA) +
  scale_x_discrete(labels = c("FALSE" = "True: typical (< threshold)", "TRUE" = "True: extreme (\u2265 threshold)")) +
  labs(title = "Classifier-predicted P(extreme) by true fire class",
       x = NULL, y = "Mean P(extreme) across 500 draws") +
  theme_minimal()

# ---- 3. Year-group check ----
clf_m[, year_group := fifelse(year %in% c(2007, 2010), "2007/2010 (many small)",
                          fifelse(year %in% c(2004, 2005), "2004/2005 (severe)", "Other years"))]

true_typical_only <- clf_m[true_extreme == FALSE]

ggplot(true_typical_only, aes(x = year_group, y = p_extreme)) +
  geom_jitter(width = 0.15, alpha = 0.4, size = 1.3, aes(color = year_group)) +
  geom_boxplot(width = 0.3, alpha = 0.3, outlier.shape = NA) +
  scale_color_manual(values = c("2007/2010 (many small)" = "#0072B2",
                                  "2004/2005 (severe)"     = "#D55E00",
                                  "Other years"             = "grey60"), guide = "none") +
  labs(title = "P(extreme) among TRULY TYPICAL (small) fires only, by year group",
       subtitle = "If 2007/2010 shows elevated P(extreme) here, the model is spuriously\ninflating some genuinely small fires toward the extreme component",
       x = NULL, y = "Mean P(extreme) across 500 draws") +
  theme_minimal()

cat("\nMean P(extreme) among true-typical fires, by year group:\n")
print(true_typical_only[, .(mean_p_extreme = mean(p_extreme), n = .N), by = year_group])

compare_component_outputs <- function(sample_result, threshold) {
  sampled  <- sample_result$sampled_draws       # n_test x n_draws
  is_ext   <- sample_result$is_extreme_draw       # n_test x n_draws, same shape

  # Flatten both matrices in parallel, tagging each (fire, draw) cell by
  # which component generated it
  dt <- data.table(
    predicted_value = as.vector(sampled),
    component       = as.vector(is_ext)
  )
  dt[, component := fifelse(component == 1, "Classified extreme", "Classified typical")]

  dt
}

component_outputs <- compare_component_outputs(samples_list[["m12_mixture_custom_truncated"]], threshold = 254.2795)

# ---- Summary stats per component ----
cat("Predicted burned area, by which component generated it (all draws pooled):\n")
print(component_outputs[, .(
  median = median(predicted_value),
  mean   = mean(predicted_value),
  p75    = quantile(predicted_value, 0.75),
  p95    = quantile(predicted_value, 0.95),
  max    = max(predicted_value),
  n      = .N
), by = component])

# ---- Overlapping density plot: are the two components' OUTPUT
# distributions actually well-separated, or largely overlapping? ----
ggplot(component_outputs[predicted_value > 0], aes(x = predicted_value, fill = component)) +
  geom_density(alpha = 0.5) +
  scale_x_log10() +
  scale_fill_manual(values = c("Classified extreme" = "#D55E00", "Classified typical" = "#0072B2")) +
  labs(title = "Predicted burned area distribution, by classified component",
       subtitle = "If the two densities overlap heavily, the extreme/typical Gamma\ncomponents are not producing meaningfully different predictions",
       x = "Predicted burned area (km\u00b2, log scale)", y = "Density", fill = NULL) +
  theme_minimal()

# ---- Direct overlap check: what fraction of "classified typical" draws
# actually exceed the extreme threshold anyway, and vice versa? ----
pct_typical_exceeding_threshold <- component_outputs[component == "Classified typical",
                                                            mean(predicted_value >= threshold)] * 100
pct_extreme_below_threshold <- component_outputs[component == "Classified extreme",
                                                        mean(predicted_value < threshold)] * 100

cat(sprintf("\n%.1f%% of draws classified TYPICAL still predicted burned area >= threshold (%.1f km\u00b2)\n",
            pct_typical_exceeding_threshold, threshold))
cat(sprintf("%.1f%% of draws classified EXTREME still predicted burned area < threshold\n",
            pct_extreme_below_threshold))
